definition_zh: 意识形态；观念体系；思想体系；（贬义）空想的教条
definition_en: a systematic set of ideas and beliefs through which a group interprets the world and justifies its actions
core_image: 把散落的想法收进一张图，排成能解释整个世界的骨架
scene: 桌上摊着一份宣言，第一页写着几条原则，后面所有条款都向它对齐。 The party's manifesto opened with a page of principles, and every later policy had to fit that ideology.
sceneCN: 这里 ideology 是「政治意识形态」（第 1 个义项：解释并规范社会的一套系统观念）；句意：该党的宣言以一页原则开篇，后来的每项政策都必须符合这套意识形态。

senses.title: Political ideology: a map for society
senses.titleCN: 政治意识形态：解释社会的一张图
senses.definition: a connected set of political ideas that explains how a society should be ordered and what its institutions should aim at
senses.definitionCN: 一套彼此关联的政治观念，解释社会应如何安排、制度应追求什么
senses.example: The two parties differ less in policy than in ideology.
senses.exampleCN: 两党的差别不在具体政策，而在意识形态。
senses.why: Ideology began as a 'science of ideas' and later came to mean the system through which a group reads the world. A political ideology is that system applied to the ordering of society.
senses.whyCN: ideology 起初意为“观念的科学”，后来指一个群体借以解读世界的体系。政治意识形态就是把这套体系用于社会安排。

senses.title: Belief system of a group
senses.definition: the shared body of assumptions and values by which any group, not only a party, makes sense of its world
senses.definitionCN: 任何群体（不只是政党）借以理解自身处境的共同预设与价值
senses.example: The profession's ideology treats long hours as proof of commitment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业的观念体系把长时间工作当作敬业的证明。
senses.why: Once ideology is a system of ideas rather than a party programme, every group that shares assumptions has one, including professions, clubs, and families.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 ideology 指观念体系而非政党纲领，任何共享预设的群体都有了一套，包括行业、社团与家庭。

senses.title: Derogatory: a doctrine out of touch
senses.definition: in a hostile use, a rigid set of ideas held regardless of evidence, or theory with no practical use
senses.definitionCN: 在敌意用法中，指不顾证据的僵硬观念，或没有实际用途的空论
senses.example: Critics dismissed the reform as ideology dressed up as science.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这项改革斥为披着科学外衣的教条。
senses.why: The word's scientific origin promised proof; when a system of ideas refuses proof, the same word becomes an accusation of blindness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的科学出身曾承诺证明；当一套观念拒绝证明时，同一个词就变成了“盲目”的指控。

senses.title: Original sense: the science of ideas
senses.definition: the original sense coined in 1796, a philosophy of the mind that derives knowledge from the senses
senses.definitionCN: 1796 年造出的本义，指从感官经验推导知识的意识哲学
senses.example: The French philosopher called his project a science of ideas, set against metaphysics.
senses.exampleCN: 那位法国哲学家把自己的工作称为“观念的科学”，与形而上学相对。
senses.why: Destutt de Tracy joined Greek idea 'form, look' to -logy 'study of' to name a new discipline. The literal meaning is a study of ideas, not a set of beliefs.
senses.whyCN: 德斯蒂·德·特拉西把希腊语 idea“形相、外观”与 -logy“学科”组合，命名一门新学问。字面义是“对观念的研究”，而不是一套信念。

senses.title: Hidden framework behind neutral practice
senses.definition: the unstated assumptions built into a practice, technology, or institution that looks neutral
senses.definitionCN: 被嵌进某种看似中立的做法、技术或制度中的未言明预设
senses.example: The claim that data speak for themselves is itself an ideology.
senses.exampleCN: “数据自己会说话”这一说法本身就是一种意识形态。
senses.why: A map is most powerful when it looks like the territory. The same system of ideas becomes ideology when its assumptions stop being noticed.
senses.whyCN: 一张地图最有力的时候，是它看起来像地面本身。当一套观念的预设不再被人注意到，它就成了意识形态。

senses.title: Corporate ideology: values as a script
senses.titleCN: 企业意识形态：价值变成话术
senses.definition: the set of values and slogans through which a company explains itself and asks its staff to behave
senses.definitionCN: 一个公司借以解释自身并要求员工照此行事的一套价值与口号
senses.example: The company's ideology praises speed and quietly punishes caution.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的观念体系赞美速度，却在暗中惩罚谨慎。
senses.why: When a set of beliefs is used to organise a workplace, the political map becomes an internal one: it marks what counts as a good employee.
senses.whyCN: 当一套信念被用来组织工作场所，政治地图就变成了内部地图：它标出什么样的人才算好员工。

senses.title: Religious or moral system
senses.definition: a religious or moral framework that explains suffering, duty, and the proper order of life
senses.definitionCN: 解释苦难、义务与生活应有秩序的一套宗教或道德框架
senses.example: The movement combined a strict moral ideology with practical charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动把严格的道德观念体系与实际慈善结合在一起。
senses.why: The same architecture of ideas can hold gods instead of parties. Whenever a group explains why the world is as it is, it is drawing this kind of map.
senses.whyCN: 同一套观念架构也可以装神明而非政党。只要一个群体解释世界为何如此，它就在画这类地图。

senses.title: The -ism label: a political programme
senses.titleCN: 以“主义”命名的政治纲领
senses.definition: a named political programme such as socialism, liberalism, or fascism, treated as a single package
senses.definitionCN: 以社会主义、自由主义、法西斯主义等命名的成套政治纲领
senses.example: By 1918 the word was used of socialism and communism themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 到 1918 年，这个词已被直接用来指社会主义与共产主义。
senses.why: English usage from 1907 first tied the term to socialist and communist writing; from 1918 the ideas and the movements merged into one label.
senses.whyCN: 英语用法从 1907 年起先把这个词与社会主义、共产主义写作绑在一起；从 1918 年起，观念与运动合并成了同一个标签。

senses.title: Dogmatic purity: ideas that cannot bend
senses.titleCN: 教条化的纯粹：不肯弯曲的观念
senses.definition: the state in which a set of ideas is defended so strictly that evidence and compromise are treated as betrayal
senses.definitionCN: 一套观念被捍卫得极其严格，以致证据与妥协都被视为背叛的状态
senses.example: The purge was justified in the name of ideological purity.
senses.exampleCN: 那场清洗以意识形态纯洁性的名义被正当化。
senses.why: A map that refuses correction stops being a guide and becomes a test of loyalty. Here ideology turns from a system of ideas into a border.
senses.whyCN: 一张拒绝修正的地图不再是指南，而变成了忠诚的检验。此时意识形态从观念体系变成了一条边界。

intro.en: Ideology is a modern coinage from two Greek pieces, idea 'form, look' and -logy 'study of'. It began as a name for a science and ended as a name for the beliefs people cannot examine. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ideology 是用两个希腊成分造的现代新词：idea“形相、外观”与 -logy“学科”。它起初是一门科学的名称，最后成了人们无法审视的信念的名称。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Coined as French idéologie, 'science of ideas', by Destutt de Tracy, for a philosophy of the mind that derives knowledge from the senses, as opposed to metaphysics.
items.cn: 由德斯蒂·德·特拉西造出法语 idéologie，意为“观念的科学”，指一种从感官经验推导知识的意识哲学，与形而上学相对。

items.en: The coinage joins idéo- 'of ideas', from Greek idea 'form, the look of a thing', with -logie, from Greek -logia 'a speaking, discourse, science', from legein 'to speak'.
items.cn: 这个新词把 idéo-“观念的”、来自希腊语 idea“形相、事物的外观”，与 -logie 结合，后者来自希腊语 -logia“言说、论述、学科”，再上溯 legein“说”。

items.en: Greek idea comes from idein 'to see', from PIE *weid- 'to see'. An idea was first a visible form, then a form held in the mind.
items.cn: 希腊语 idea 来自 idein“看见”，再上溯原始印欧语 *weid-“看见”。观念最初是可见的形相，后来成为心中的形相。

items.en: Destutt published his Eléments d'idéologie in these years, fixing the word in its learned, neutral sense.
items.cn: 德斯蒂在这一时期出版《观念学原理》，把这个词固定在学术性的中立义上。

items.en: The sense 'systematic set of ideas, doctrines through which the world is interpreted' appears in English by 1907, earliest in socialist and communist writing; from 1918 it names socialism and communism themselves, and later fascism.
items.cn: “借以解释世界的系统观念与学说”这一义项在 1907 年前后进入英语，最早见于社会主义与共产主义写作；从 1918 年起，它直接指社会主义与共产主义本身，后来又指法西斯主义。

items.en: The term became omnipresent only after Marx's The German Ideology and Mannheim's Ideology and Utopia appeared between the world wars. Ideological is recorded from 1797, and ideologue names the person who lives inside the map.
items.cn: 这个词要到马克思《德意志意识形态》与曼海姆《意识形态与乌托邦》在两次世界大战之间问世之后才无处不在。ideological 从 1797 年起有记录，ideologue 则指住在这张地图里的人。

note.en: The first group separates idea, ideal, the adjective, and the person from ideology; the second group compares other names for sets of beliefs.
note.cn: 第一组把 idea、ideal、形容词与“人”同 ideology 分开；第二组比较其他表示“信念集合”的说法。

entries.definition: a thought, concept, or plan in the mind. It is one unit; ideology is the system that arranges many such units into a world picture.
entries.definitionCN: 心中的一个想法、概念或计划。它是一个单位；ideology 则是把许多这样的单位排成世界图景的体系。

entries.definition: a standard of perfection, or the best possible form of something. An ideal is what a belief aims at; an ideology is the whole frame that contains both the aim and its justification.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的标准，或某物可能达到的最佳形态。ideal 是信念所指向的目标；ideology 是同时容纳目标与理由的整个框架。

entries.definition: relating to an ideology. It describes how something is driven by a set of ideas, as in an ideological dispute, rather than naming the set itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与意识形态有关的。它描述某事如何由一套观念驱动，如意识形态争论，而不是命名这套观念本身。

entries.definition: a person who holds a doctrine rigidly and defends it. It is usually hostile: the ideologue is the one who will not look outside the map.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬坚持并捍卫一套学说的人。它通常带敌意：意识形态者就是不肯往地图外面看的那个人。

entries.definition: a set of principles taught or officially held, often by a church or a state. Doctrine stresses authority and instruction; ideology stresses the whole way of seeing the world.
entries.definitionCN: 被教授或官方持有的一套原则，常属教会或国家。doctrine 强调权威与教导；ideology 强调整套看世界的方式。

entries.definition: the connected beliefs a person or group holds. It is the plain, neutral phrase; ideology is the academic and often political word for the same architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体所持的相互关联的信念。它是朴素中性的说法；ideology 是同一架构的学术用词，且常带政治色彩。

entries.definition: the overall way a person or culture sees existence. A worldview may be private and philosophical; an ideology is more organised, shared, and acted upon.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或文化看待存在的整体方式。worldview 可以是私人的、哲学的；ideology 则更有组织、更共享、更被付诸行动。

entries.definition: a principle laid down as unquestionably true. Dogma is one brick; ideology is the building, and calling it dogma is already the hostile sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被规定为不容置疑的原则。dogma 是一块砖；ideology 是整座建筑，而把它称为 dogma 时，已经用上了贬义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek idea 'form, look' plus -logy 'study of', and the family ideological / ideologue / ideologist.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 idea“形相、外观”加 -logy“学科”，以及 ideological／ideologue／ideologist 词族。

normal.en: idea means 'form or look' and -logy means 'study of'. Ideology was literally the study of ideas before it became the ideas themselves.
normal.cn: idea 表示“形相或外观”，-logy 表示“对……的研究”。ideology 字面上是“对观念的研究”，后来才变成观念本身。

normal.en: The -logy ending also builds biology, psychology and theology, so ideology belongs to the same family of 'named fields of study'.
normal.cn: -logy 也构成 biology、psychology、theology，所以 ideology 属于同一类“被命名的学问领域”。

normal.en: Ideological is the adjective, ideologue is the person, and ideologist is the person who studies the system.
normal.cn: ideological 是形容词，ideologue 是信奉者，ideologist 是研究这套体系的人。

normal.en: Do not confuse ideal with idea: an ideal is the perfect standard, an idea is one thought, and an ideology is the frame that holds many thoughts together.
normal.cn: 不要把 ideal 与 idea 混同：ideal 是完美标准，idea 是一个想法，ideology 是把许多想法收在一起的那个框架。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1796 as a neutral science, and only after 1907 did it become the name of political belief systems.
normal.cn: 这个词 1796 年被造出时是一门中立科学，直到 1907 年之后才成为政治信念体系的名称。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of loose notes. Ideology is the moment someone draws a frame around them and says: these belong together and explain everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠散乱的笔记。ideology 就是有人给它们画上一个框，并说：这些属于同一体，能解释一切的那一刻。

abstract.en: The frame can hold a party, a profession, a company, or a church. Whatever it holds, its power comes from being mistaken for the world itself.
abstract.cn: 这个框可以装一个政党、一个行业、一家公司或一座教堂。不论装什么，它的力量都来自被误当成世界本身。

abstract.en: A frame that can be revised stays a map. A frame that cannot be revised becomes a border, and crossing it is treated as betrayal.
abstract.cn: 可以修改的框仍是地图；不能修改的框变成边界，越过它就被当成背叛。

examples.en: The textbook presents its own assumptions as neutral method, which is how ideology usually hides.
examples.cn: 这本教科书把自己的预设呈现为中立的方法，意识形态通常就是这样藏起来的。

examples.en: She studied how colonial ideology shaped the maps children were given.
examples.cn: 她研究殖民意识形态如何塑造发给孩子们的地图。

examples.en: Calling every conviction an ideology makes it impossible to argue with any of them.
examples.cn: 把一切信念都称为意识形态，会让人无法与其中任何一种辩论。

dict_mnemonic.text: “爱迪欧乐吉”——爱迪欧（ideo）把一堆想法收进一个乐（logy）高音喇叭，对着全世界广播 → ideology 意识形态、观念体系

root: 源自希腊语 idea“形相、外观”+ -logia“言说、学科”，1796 年由法语 idéologie 造出，核心是“把零散观念收成一套能解释世界的体系”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ideology, all grown from one structure: scattered ideas are gathered into a frame, and that frame is then used to read the world, justify action, or shut out doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: ideology 的九个义项都从同一个结构长出来：零散的想法被收进一个框架，这个框架随后被用来解读世界、为行动辩护，或把怀疑关在门外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame drawn around many ideas so that they explain a whole world.
core.cn: 核心意象：给许多想法画上一个框，使它们能解释整个世界。

chain: A WAY TO READ THE WORLD

branches.en: POLITICS: the frame becomes a party programme, and the programme acquires an -ism label.
branches.cn: 政治：框架变成政党纲领，纲领再获得一个“主义”标签。

branches.en: GROUP LIFE: professions, companies, and religions each read their world through their own frame.
branches.cn: 群体生活：行业、公司与宗教各自用自己的一套框架解读世界。

branches.en: RIGIDITY: when the frame refuses evidence and compromise, it turns from doctrine into an accusation and then into a border.
branches.cn: 僵硬：当框架拒绝证据与妥协，它就从学说变成指控，再变成边界。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the coined sense was a neutral study of ideas, not a set of beliefs.
branches.cn: 起源：造词时的义项是对观念的中立研究，而不是一套信念。

branches.en: HIDDEN FRAME: the system works best when its assumptions pass unnoticed, like a map mistaken for ground.
branches.cn: 隐藏的框架：当预设不被人注意时，这套体系最有效，就像地图被当成地面。

intro.en: Ideology is a modern compound of two Greek elements: idea 'form, look' and -logy 'study or discourse'. English adds -ical, -ly, -logue, and -ist to build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: ideology 是由两个希腊成分构成的现代复合词：idea“形相、外观”与 -logy“研究或论述”。英语再加上 -ical、-ly、-logue、-ist 构成整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin idea was borrowed from Greek idea 'form, look', and Medieval Latin -logia came from Greek -logia, from logos 'word, speech'. The elements are Greek, but they reached modern European languages through Latin and French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 idea 借自希腊语 idea“形相、外观”，中世纪拉丁语 -logia 来自希腊语 -logia，再上溯 logos“词、言说”。成分是希腊的，但它们是经拉丁语与法语进入现代欧洲语言的。

items.meaning: a system of ideas through which the world is interpreted
items.meaningCN: 解释世界的观念体系（ideo- 观念的 + -logy 学科）
items.example: The film examines the ideology behind urban planning.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片审视城市规划背后的意识形态。

items.meaning: more than one system of ideas
items.meaningCN: 多套观念体系（辅音加 y 结尾变 y 为 i 加 -es）
items.example: Competing ideologies shaped the new constitution.
items.exampleCN: 彼此竞争的各种意识形态塑造了新宪法。

items.meaning: driven by or belonging to an ideology
items.meaningCN: 意识形态的；由观念体系驱动的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The split was personal before it became ideological.
items.exampleCN: 这场分裂先是人际的，后来才变成意识形态的。

items.meaning: from the standpoint of an ideology
items.meaningCN: 从意识形态立场上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two proposals are ideologically opposed but practically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两项提案在观念上对立，在实际操作上却相似。

items.meaning: a rigid defender of a doctrine
items.meaningCN: 教条捍卫者；意识形态者（-logue 表示说话者）
items.example: He was a party ideologue who never met a compromise he liked.
items.exampleCN: 他是个党的意识形态者，从不喜欢任何妥协。

items.meaning: one who studies or formulates ideologies
items.meaningCN: 研究或制定思想体系的人（-ist 表示人）
items.example: The regime relied on ideologists to rewrite the textbooks.
items.exampleCN: 该政权依靠意识形态专家改写教科书。

items.structure: Greek idea 'form, look', from idein 'to see'
items.meaning: a thought or concept in the mind

items.exampleCN: 这个想法是她在公交车上想到的。

items.meaningCN: 理想；完美标准（-al 构成形容词与名词）

items.exampleCN: 这个方案更像一种理想，而不是一份日程。

items.meaningCN: 把某物理想化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The memoir idealizes a childhood it barely describes.
items.exampleCN: 这本回忆录把它几乎没怎么描述的童年理想化了。

items.meaningCN: 生物学（bio- 生命 + -logy 学科）
items.example: She took biology as her second subject.
items.exampleCN: 她把生物学选为第二专业。

items.exampleCN: 心理学曾作为哲学的一部分被教授。

senses.title: To pay no attention
senses.definition: to give no attention to something

senses.title: To refuse to acknowledge

senses.definitionCN: 拒绝招呼或回应某人
senses.example: She knocked, but the people inside ignored her.

senses.why: Here the object is a person asking for a response.

senses.title: To disregard deliberately

senses.definitionCN: 行为上仿佛规则或事实不重要
senses.example: They ignored the rules and kept going.

items.en: Ignore also means to snub a person.

definition_zh: 非法的；违法的；不合法的
definition_en: forbidden by law or by official rules, and punishable if done
core_image: 大楼门口一块被红笔划掉的车位牌，写着此处禁止停车
scene: 市中心的巷口立着一块新做的牌子。Parking there is illegal after eight in the evening, so drivers keep moving past it.
sceneCN: 这里 illegal 指「非法的、违法的」（第 1 个义项：法律明令禁止），句意是晚上八点后在那里停车属违法，于是司机们一路开过去。画面里有巷口、新牌子和不肯停下的车。

pos.zh: 形容词：非法的、违法的、不合法的

collocations.phrase: it is illegal to do something

collocations.zh: 严格禁止的、绝对违法的

senses.title: Forbidden by law
senses.definition: against the law and punishable by the courts
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律、会被法院处罚的
senses.example: It is illegal to sell alcohol to children.
senses.exampleCN: 向儿童出售酒类是违法的。
senses.why: The prefix in- here works as a pure negative, so the word simply says that a thing does not fall inside the law.
senses.whyCN: 这里的前缀表否定，词义就是「这件事不在法律许可的范围之内」。

senses.title: Against the rules of a sport or game
senses.definition: not allowed by the rules of a game or competition
senses.definitionCN: 违反比赛规则的
senses.example: The referee ruled that the tackle was illegal.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判判定这次抢球属于犯规。
senses.why: Sport has its own rule book, and since the word points at any codified rule, it slid easily from courts of law to fields of play.
senses.whyCN: 体育有自己的规则册，而这个词指向一切成文规则，于是自然从法庭滑到了球场。

senses.title: Not officially approved
senses.definition: done without official permission, especially in building or trade
senses.definitionCN: 未获官方许可而做的，尤指建筑或经营
senses.example: An illegal extension was built onto the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 房子后面加建了一间未经批准的屋子。
senses.why: Modern life adds licences and permits to law, and anything done outside them borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 现代生活给法律添上执照与许可，凡在许可之外做的事也借用同一个词。

intro.en: Illegal joins a Latin negative prefix to the Latin word for law; it entered English through French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: illegal 由拉丁语否定前缀与拉丁语「法律」一词合成，中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Lex, legis meant law, whether a statute or a binding custom of the community.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex、属格 legis 意为「法律」，既指成文法，也指共同体约束性的习俗。

items.en: Legalis described what belonged to law and was lawful, a word already carrying a clear yes or no.
items.cn: legalis 形容「属于法律的、合法的」，本身已带有明确的是非判断。

items.en: Adding the negative in-, scribes formed illegals to name what fell outside the law.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 in- 后，抄写者们造出 illegals，用来指法律之外的事。

items.en: French carried the form as illegal, and its legal clerks used it constantly in court records.
items.cn: 法语以 illegal 的形式承下此词，司法文书里频繁使用。

items.en: English took it up in the sixteenth century and broadened it to rules of sports, trades and building.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪收入该词，并把适用范围扩展到体育规则、行业与建筑。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the il- family born from the same negative prefix; the near-meaning group collects other strong words for what is not allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由否定前缀 il- 生成的家族词；近义组收其他表示「不被允许」的强词。

entries.definition: Not following reason; it shares the same il- prefix and the same negative force.
entries.definitionCN: 不合逻辑的；共用同一个 il- 否定前缀与否定意味。

entries.definition: Impossible to read, built with the same prefix but applied to writing.
entries.definitionCN: 难以辨认的，前缀相同但用于书写。

entries.definition: Not allowed or not valid, a close cousin that adds the idea of legitimacy.
entries.definitionCN: 不正当的、无效的，多了一层「正当性」的意思。

entries.definition: Not permitted by law, the plainest native synonym of illegal.
entries.definitionCN: 不合法的，是 illegal 最直白的同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to crime; stronger, since it names punishable wrongdoing.
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪的；语气更重，因为它直接指向应受刑罚的恶行。

entries.definition: Not allowed by someone in authority, often a household or a school.
entries.definitionCN: 被禁止的，多用于当权者的规定，如家中或校内。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin law root and the loud negative prefix to fix the spelling and the meaning together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借拉丁语「法律」词根与显眼的否定前缀，把拼写与词义一起钉住。

normal.en: il- is a negative prefix, and legal is law, so illegal is literally not legal.
normal.cn: il- 是否定前缀，legal 是法律上的，所以 illegal 字面上就是「不合法」。

normal.en: The double l is the trick of spelling: the in- of negation folds into the l of legal.
normal.cn: 拼写难点在双 l：否定的 in- 在 l 前同化成 il-。

normal.en: The same il- hides in illogical and illegible, so any il- word is a no.
normal.cn: 同一个 il- 也藏在 illogical 与 illegible 里，凡以 il- 开头都是「不」。

normal.en: Say it with the stress on the second beat: il-LEE-gal, like LEAR in legal.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二拍：il-LEE-gal，与 legal 里的 LE- 呼应。

normal.en: Remember the traffic sign with the red circle and a slash: that circle is illegal in picture form.
normal.cn: 记住交通牌上带斜杠的红圈：那个圈就是 illegal 的图解。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in chalk around the law; everything outside the line is not banned by nature, only by that line.
abstract.cn: 想象用粉笔绕法律画了一圈：圈外的事本身并非天理不容，只是被那条线挡住。

abstract.en: The word never denies that an act happens; it only reports that the law refuses to approve of it.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不否认事情真的发生了，只说法律不肯点头。

abstract.en: A prefix as small as two letters can turn a permission into a prohibition, which shows how thin the line between yes and no is.
abstract.cn: 两个字母的前缀就能把允许翻成禁止，由此可见允与禁之间的界线有多薄。

examples.en: It is illegal to drive without a licence.
examples.cn: 无证驾驶是违法的。

examples.en: The factory was fined for illegal waste dumping.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因非法倾倒废物被罚款。

examples.en: Officials promised to close the illegal market within a week.
examples.cn: 官员承诺一周内取缔这个非法市场。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: what the law forbids, what the rules of a game forbid, and what lacks official approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：法律禁止的、比赛规则禁止的，以及缺少官方批准的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line drawn around the law, with everything beyond it closed off.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕法律画出一道红线，线外之事全部封闭。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: selling to children or driving unlicensed is against statute.
branches.cn: 法律线：向儿童售酒、无照驾驶都触犯法条。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: a rough tackle is illegal under the rules of football.
branches.cn: 球场线：足球里粗野抢球按规则属于犯规。

branches.en: THE PERMIT LINE: an extension built without papers is illegal even if nobody complains.
branches.cn: 许可线：没有手续的加建，即使无人投诉也属违建。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT LINE: both senses need an authority to say no.
branches.cn: 裁决线：两种用法都需要一个权威来判定「不行」。

branches.en: THE PAPER LINE: licences and statutes are the documents the word quietly points at.
branches.cn: 文书线：执照与法规正是这个词默默指向的纸面依据。

intro.en: Illegal is a clean prefix-plus-root pattern: a Latin negative, a Latin law root, and English endings built on both.
intro.cn: illegal 是干净的前缀加词根结构：拉丁语否定前缀、拉丁语法律词根，以及在这两者上长出的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The negative in- and the law root lex are both attested in Latin, and the assimilation of n to l is a regular sound change.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀 in- 与法律词根 lex 在拉丁语中都有文献，n 同化为 l 是规律性的语音变化。

items.exampleCN: 同一个前缀也见于 illogical。

items.exampleCN: 这份合同合法且具约束力。

definition_zh: 文盲状态；不识字；（某一领域的）基本无知
definition_en: the inability to read and write, or a lack of the basic knowledge needed in a particular field
core_image: 一张贴在诊所墙上的通知，字行密密麻麻，一个人站在前面反复打量却无法读出内容
scene: 诊所墙上贴着一张密密麻麻的通知，一位老人站在前面反复打量，最后转身问护士。Illiteracy kept him from reading the dosage on the label himself.
sceneCN: 这里指「不识字的状态」（第 1 个义项：缺乏读写能力）；句意为他因不识字，无法自己读出标签上的用量说明。可辨识物件：通知、字行、老人、标签。

pos.zh: 文盲状态；不识字（通常不可数）

senses.title: Inability to read and write
senses.definition: the condition of being unable to read or write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 无法读懂或写出简短浅近文字的状态
senses.example: Illiteracy closed doors that a signature would have opened.
senses.exampleCN: 不识字关上了那些本可由一个签名打开的门。
senses.why: the noun is the negative twin of literacy, so its core is the plain absence of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是「读写能力」的否定孪生词，其核心就是字母的缺席。

senses.title: The measured rate in a population
senses.definition: the share of a population that cannot read, treated as a figure for reports
senses.definitionCN: 不能读写者在人口中的比例，被当作报告用的数字
senses.example: Illiteracy fell by a third in the decade after the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 扫盲运动之后的十年里，文盲比例下降了三分之一。
senses.why: governments needed a number to track, so the condition became a statistic under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要一个可追踪的数字，于是这种状态以同一名称变成统计量。

senses.title: Functional illiteracy
senses.titleCN: 能认字却读不懂日常文书
senses.definition: the state of having some schooling yet being unable to use print in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 虽上过学，却无法在日常生活中实际运用文字的状态
senses.example: Functional illiteracy hides behind a school certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 实用性文盲常常藏在毕业证后面。
senses.why: the word widened from absence of letters to inability to use them, which is harder to see.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「不认识字母」扩展到「不会使用文字」，后者更难察觉。

senses.title: Digital illiteracy
senses.definition: the lack of basic competence with computers and online services
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏使用计算机与网络服务的基本能力
senses.example: Digital illiteracy excludes people from services that moved online.
senses.exampleCN: 数字文盲使一些人被排除在已搬到线上的服务之外。
senses.why: screens introduced a new set of signs, and the old negative noun was reused for them.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕带来一套新的符号，这个旧的否定名词因此被用于其上。

senses.title: Scientific or numerical illiteracy
senses.definition: the lack of the basic ideas needed to judge scientific or quantitative claims
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏判断科学或数量主张所需的基本概念
senses.example: Scientific illiteracy makes a misleading chart hard to challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 科学盲使人难以质疑一张误导性的图表。
senses.why: a field's basic vocabulary is the alphabet one must know, so its absence takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 某领域的基本词汇就是必须认识的字母，其缺席因此沿用同一名称。

senses.title: Illiteracy as a policy problem
senses.titleCN: 作为公共政策议题的文盲现象
senses.definition: the condition viewed as a social problem that states try to measure and reduce
senses.definitionCN: 被国家试图测量并减少的社会问题
senses.example: The ministry treated illiteracy as an obstacle to economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 该部把文盲问题视为经济增长的障碍。
senses.why: once the condition is counted, it also becomes something to be governed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种状态被计数，它也就成了治理对象。

senses.title: Illiteracy in a region or group
senses.titleCN: 某地区或群体的文盲状况
senses.definition: the extent of the condition among a named population, such as rural women
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定人群（如农村妇女）中的普遍程度
senses.example: Illiteracy among older women remained the highest in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 年长女性的文盲程度仍是全国最高。
senses.why: once counted, the condition can be compared across groups, and the name travels with the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被计数，这种状态便可在群体间比较，名称也随之进入比较。

senses.title: Ignorance of a field's basic codes
senses.titleCN: 对某领域基本规则的无知（引申义）
senses.definition: a figurative lack of the basic vocabulary needed to take part in a field
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地缺乏参与某一领域所需的基本词汇
senses.example: Economic illiteracy made the debate impossible to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 经济盲使这场辩论根本无法跟上。
senses.why: the metaphor is complete once 'letters' means any system of signs a participant must read.
senses.whyCN: 当「字母」泛指参与者必须读懂的任一符号系统时，这个比喻就完整了。

intro.en: Illiteracy is the negative noun matching literacy, built on Latin illitteratus 'unlettered', itself in- 'not' plus litteratus 'lettered'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是与「读写能力」相配的否定名词，建于拉丁 illitteratus「不识字的」之上，后者由否定前缀加 litteratus「写有字母的」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural writings or a letter. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数指著作或书信。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus 'lettered, learned' was formed with an ending meaning 'provided with'.
items.cn: litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」由表「带有」的词尾构成。

items.en: The negating prefix in- assimilated to the following consonant, giving illitteratus 'unlettered, unlearned'.
items.cn: 否定前缀因后接辅音而同化，形成 illitteratus「不识字的、无学问的」。

items.en: English formed the noun in the seventeenth century, when schooling and printing made the lack of letters a visible social fact.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪构成这个名词，当时学校教育与印刷使「不识字」成为显见的社会事实。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word also named a rate to be counted, and from the late twentieth it was extended to digital and scientific fields.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词也指可计数的比率；二十世纪后期又扩展到数字与科学领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and the earliest printed use of the English noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个英语名词最早的印刷书证年代亦不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same root that differ only in endings; group two holds words naming a lack of knowledge.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、只差词尾的词形；第二组是表示知识缺乏的词。

entries.definition: Describes someone unable to read, or names such a person; the noun names the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不能读写的某人，或指这样的人；名词则指这种状态。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write; the two nouns differ only by a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指读写能力；两个名词只差一个前缀。

entries.definition: Means 'following the exact words' and has no negative force at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，完全没有否定含义。

entries.definition: Able to read and write; it is the exact opposite of the adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 指能读写，与形容词形式正好相反。

entries.definition: A general lack of knowledge; illiteracy is the specific lack of reading and writing.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指缺乏知识；文盲特指缺乏读写能力。

entries.definition: The lack of basic competence with numbers, coined as the counterpart of numeracy.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏数字基本能力，是仿「数字能力」造出的反面词。

entries.definition: An older literary word for uneducated; it is close but belongs to formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 较古雅的说法，指未受教育，意思接近但属正式书面语。

entries.definition: Having only fragmentary reading and writing; it sits between the two poles.
entries.definitionCN: 指读写能力零碎，处于两极之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is literacy wearing a prefix of denial, so the pair is learned together.
normal.cn: 这个词就是戴上否定前缀的「读写能力」，两个词宜成对记。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern fields: digital illiteracy, scientific illiteracy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代领域：数字文盲、科学盲。

normal.en: The condition is also a number, which is why the phrase illiteracy rate exists.
normal.cn: 这种状态也会变成数字，因此有「文盲率」这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs illiterate, literacy, literate, semiliterate.
normal.cn: 同族包括「不识字的」「读写能力」「识字的」「半文盲的」。

normal.en: Functional illiteracy is the hidden kind: a certificate without usable skills.
normal.cn: 实用性文盲是隐藏的一类：有证书，却没有可用技能。

abstract.en: Picture a notice whose lines turn into a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张通知，上面的字行变成一扇锁住的门。

abstract.en: Picture a map with no names, so every road looks the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有地名的地图，每条路看起来都一样。

abstract.en: Picture a key that exists but cannot be found when the door is closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙确实存在，却在门要关时找不到。

examples.en: Illiteracy among rural women fell sharply once village classes opened.
examples.cn: 乡村夜校开办后，农村女性的文盲状况迅速下降。

examples.en: Functional illiteracy can survive years of schooling.
examples.cn: 实用性文盲可以在多年学校教育之后依然存在。

examples.en: Scientific illiteracy leaves people unable to judge a risk for themselves.
examples.cn: 科学盲使人无法自行判断风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一里特乐西」——一个字母都认不得，里外都乐不起来，这就是文盲状态。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」加表「带有」的词尾成 litteratus「识字的」，再加否定前缀构成 illitteratus「不识字的」；英语十七世纪由此构成 illiteracy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an absence: letters, then usable print, then the tools of a screen age, then the codes of science and of whole fields, until the word finally names any basic ignorance a society decides to count.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一种缺席：先是字母，再是可用的文字，然后是屏幕时代的工具，接着是科学与各领域的规则，最后指社会决定加以计数的任何基本无知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dense notice on a wall that refuses to become words.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上密密麻麻的通知，始终不肯变成可读的词。

branches.en: THE BASE ABSENCE: not knowing letters is the oldest and plainest layer.
branches.cn: 基底缺席：不认识字母是最古老也最朴素的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED AND GOVERNED: once measured, the condition becomes a target for policy.
branches.cn: 被计数与被治理：一旦被测量，这种状态就成为政策目标。

branches.en: PRINT WITHOUT USE: schooling can leave people unable to handle real paperwork.
branches.cn: 有字却无用：学校教育可能仍留下不会处理实际文书的人。

branches.en: NEW CODES: screens and scientific claims each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新密码：屏幕与科学主张各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: WHO AND WHERE: the condition is unevenly spread, and it can be figurative as well.
branches.cn: 谁与何处：这种状态分布不均，也可作比喻用法。

intro.en: The word is the negative member of a small family built on a Latin root for a letter.
intro.cn: 这个词是建在拉丁语表「字母」词根上的一个小词族中的否定成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, literature and literal; litteratus gives literate, and with a negating prefix it gives illitteratus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 衍生出「字母」「文学」与「字面的」；litteratus 衍生出「识字的」，加否定前缀则成 illitteratus。

items.example: The prefix assimilates to the next sound, which is why it appears as il-.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀会与后一个音同化，写作同化后的形式。

items.example: The root names the smallest unit of print.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指印刷文字的最小单位。

items.example: The adjective describes a person furnished with letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述一个「带着字母」的人。

items.example: The negative form entered English through learned Latin.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式经学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: The label was once used for anyone outside formal schooling.
items.exampleCN: 这个标签曾用于任何未受正规教育的人。

items.example: Illiteracy was treated as a national problem.
items.exampleCN: 文盲被当作一项国家问题。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write
items.example: Literacy programs were funded by the province.
items.exampleCN: 识字项目由省里拨款。
半文盲读者需要更简单的表格。

definition_en: the state of being unwell, or a particular disease that a person has
core_image: 床头柜上摊开的温水和几板药片，窗帘半掩着
scene: 孩子连着两晚发烧，母亲请了假守在家里。The illness lasted a week, so the whole family learned to move quietly around the sickroom.
sceneCN: 这里 illness 指「疾病、生病」（第 1 个义项：身体不健康的状态），句意是这场病持续了一周，全家人学会了在病床边轻手轻脚。画面里有温水、药片和半掩的窗帘。

senses.title: The state of being unwell
senses.definition: the condition of being in poor health over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内身体健康不佳的状况
senses.example: His illness kept him away from work for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病让他一个月没能上班。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the adjective ill into an abstract state, so the word names a condition rather than a single symptom.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词 ill 变成抽象状态，因此这个词指的是一段处境，而非单个症状。

senses.title: A particular disease
senses.definition: a specific sickness with a name, such as measles or diabetes
senses.definitionCN: 有名称的某种具体病症，如麻疹或糖尿病
senses.example: She suffers from a rare blood illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她患有一种罕见的血液病。
senses.why: Once people began diagnosing in detail, the state word was reused for each named disease the doctors could identify.
senses.whyCN: 当诊断细化之后，这个表示状态的词就被借去指医生能一一命名的病症。

senses.title: A period of sickness
senses.definition: a stretch of time during which someone is ill
senses.definitionCN: 一个人患病的这段时间
senses.example: During his illness the neighbours brought meals every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 在他患病期间，邻居们每晚都送来饭菜。
senses.why: English often measures states by their duration, and so the word is used for the span as well as the condition.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用时长来衡量状态，于是这个词既指病情，也指那一整段时间。

intro.en: Illness is an Old Norse word dressed with an English ending: ill came from the north and -ness is native.
intro.cn: illness 是古诺斯语词根加英语词尾：ill 来自北方，-ness 是本土成分。

items.en: The Scandinavian adjective illr meant bad or evil, covering both harm and moral wrong.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚语形容词 illr 意为「坏的、恶的」，兼指伤害与道德之恶。

items.en: English already had -nes, a suffix that turned adjectives into names for their states.
items.cn: 英语早已有 -nes 这一词尾，能把形容词变成表示状态的抽象名词。

items.en: After the Norse settlers, ill settled into English and gradually narrowed towards poor health.
items.cn: 北欧移民进入英格兰后，ill 扎根英语，词义逐渐收窄到健康不佳。

items.en: Combining ill with -ness gave illness, first as wickedness and later as sickness.
items.cn: ill 与 -ness 结合成 illness，最初表「邪恶」，后来转为「疾病」。

items.en: Medical writing fixed illness as the standard abstract noun for poor health and named diseases.
items.cn: 医学写作把 illness 固定为表示不健康与具体病症的标准抽象名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -ness words built on short adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers words for sickness itself.
note.cn: 形近组收其他由短形容词加 -ness 构成的词；近义组收表示疾病本身的词。

entries.definition: The state of being weak, made the same way from a short adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱、弱点，构成方式相同。

entries.definition: The state of being sad, another abstract noun on -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 悲伤，又一个 -ness 抽象名词。

entries.definition: The state of doing nothing, close in shape to illness.
entries.definitionCN: 闲散、无所事事，形状与 illness 相近。

entries.definition: A medical condition with identifiable signs, often more clinical than illness.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确体征的疾病，比 illness 更偏医学。

entries.definition: The state of being sick, or vomiting; plainer and often physical.
entries.definitionCN: 生病、恶心呕吐；更口语，也常指生理反应。

entries.definition: A minor illness that keeps troubling someone over time.
entries.definitionCN: 常年缠人的小毛病。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the suffix -ness, the Norse origin, and the everyday details of being sick in bed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用上 -ness 词尾、北欧来源以及卧病在床的日常细节。

normal.en: ill is the adjective, -ness makes the state, so illness is the condition of being ill.
normal.cn: ill 是形容词，-ness 把状态名词化，illness 就是「生病这件事」。

normal.en: Spell it with double l, just as in ill, plus ness: illness, four letters then four.
normal.cn: 拼写用双 l，与 ill 一致，再加 ness：前半四个字母，后半也是四个。

normal.en: The word came from the north with the Vikings, so the l's are not silent.
normal.cn: 这个词随北欧人从北方而来，其中的 l 要发出来。

normal.en: Only two syllables, stress the first: ILL-ness.
normal.cn: 只有两个音节，重音在前：ILL-ness。

normal.en: Think of a sick note on an office desk: the paper names an illness, not a person.
normal.cn: 想想办公桌上的一张病假条：纸上写的是病名，不是人名。

abstract.en: The oldest meaning of the root was evil, not sickness, which shows how a moral word can drift into medicine.
abstract.cn: 这个词根最古老的意思是「恶」而非「病」，可见道德词如何漂进医学。

abstract.en: A suffix of four letters turns a passing adjective into a whole season of life, which is why illness feels longer than ill.
abstract.cn: 四个字母的词尾把一时的形容词变成人生的一整段，所以 illness 听起来比 ill 更长。

abstract.en: The word describes a condition, never a blame; it holds a person without judging one.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述的是处境，从不追究过错；它承载一个人，却不评判一个人。

examples.en: She took three days off because of illness.
examples.cn: 她因病请了三天假。

examples.en: Mental illness deserves the same care as physical illness.
examples.cn: 精神疾病应当得到与身体疾病同样的关怀。

examples.en: He never spoke about his long illness at work.
examples.cn: 他在单位从不谈自己长期的病。

dict_mnemonic.text: ill 生病的 + ness 状态名词尾——生病的状态，即疾病

root: 古诺斯语 illr「坏的、恶的」→ 中古英语 ill「不佳、有病」，加本土词尾 -nes（今 -ness）构成表示状态的抽象名词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the state of poor health, a named disease, and the period it lasts.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：健康不佳的状态、有名称的具体疾病，以及疾病持续的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of water and tablets on a bedside table with the curtain half drawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头柜上一杯水和几板药片，窗帘半掩。

branches.en: THE STATE LINE: the word names a stretch of poor health, not one symptom.
branches.cn: 状态线：这个词指一段时间的不健康，而非单个症状。

branches.en: THE DIAGNOSIS LINE: doctors attach the word to named diseases.
branches.cn: 诊断线：医生把这个词挂到有名字的病症上。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: during his illness marks a period with a beginning and an end.
branches.cn: 日历线：患病期间标记出一段有始有终的时间。

branches.en: THE BED LINE: rest, medicine and quiet neighbours all belong to it.
branches.cn: 病床线：休息、药物与轻声的邻居都属于它。

branches.en: THE WORK LINE: a sick note certifies illness so the office accepts it.
branches.cn: 单位线：病假条为 illness 作证，单位才会认可。

intro.en: Illness is a short Norse adjective plus a native abstract suffix, one of the most ordinary patterns in English.
intro.cn: illness 是一个简短的北欧形容词加本土抽象词尾，属于英语最普通的构词方式。

latinIntro.en: Nothing here is Latin: the adjective travelled from Old Norse and the suffix is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这两部分都不来自拉丁语：形容词来自古诺斯语，词尾属日耳曼语。

items.example: He felt ill after the long journey.
items.exampleCN: 长途旅行后他觉得不适。

items.example: Kindness and darkness use it too.
items.exampleCN: kindness 与 darkness 也用这个词尾。
疾病迫使她休息。

items.example: He had several illnesses as a child.
items.exampleCN: 他幼年得过好几种病。
病让他待在家里。
她抱病的父亲需要照料。
整个冬天他都很健康。
troublesome 属这一类。

definition_zh: 阐明；说明；演示；给（书）加插图
definition_en: to make something clear by giving examples or pictures, or to add pictures to a book
core_image: 黑板上被老师用红粉笔圈出的一幅示意图
scene: 物理老师讲浮力时先放下教材，转身在黑板上画了一条船。She used two arrows to illustrate how the water pushed the hull upward.
sceneCN: 这里 illustrate 是「阐明、说明」（第 1 个义项：用例子或图示把道理讲清），句意是她用两个箭头说明水如何把船体托起。画面里有黑板、红粉笔和一艘简笔画的船。

pos.zh: 动词：阐明、说明；给书加插图

senses.title: To make an idea clear
senses.definition: to explain something by giving examples or by showing how it works
senses.definitionCN: 用例子或演示来说明某事
senses.example: Let me illustrate the rule with a simple case.
senses.exampleCN: 让我用个简单的例子说明这条规则。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to light up, and an example does exactly that for an abstract idea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根本是「照亮」，而例子对抽象观念所做的正是照亮。

senses.title: To add pictures to a text
senses.definition: to supply drawings or photographs for a book or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 为书籍或杂志提供插图或照片
senses.example: A young artist illustrated the whole storybook.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年轻画家为整本故事书画了插图。
senses.why: Pictures make a text bright and easy to grasp, so the same verb was extended from words to images.
senses.whyCN: 图画使文字明朗易懂，于是同一个动词从说明扩展到配图。

senses.title: To be an example of
senses.definition: to serve as a clear instance that shows a general fact
senses.definitionCN: 作为能说明普遍事实的明确例子
senses.example: His career illustrates how talent and luck combine.
senses.exampleCN: 他的经历说明了天赋与运气如何结合。
senses.why: When a case makes a truth visible, English lets the case itself become the subject and light up the claim.
senses.whyCN: 当一个事例让道理显现时，英语就让这个事例作主语，替主张打光。

intro.en: Illustrate goes back to a Latin verb for lighting up, and that image of light still sits inside the word.
intro.cn: illustrate 可追溯到一个意为「照亮」的拉丁动词，光的意象至今留在词里。

items.en: Lustrare meant to light up or make bright, and was used of light striking a dark place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lustrare 意为照亮、使明亮，常指光照进暗处。

items.en: Illustrare strengthened it: to throw light on, and figuratively to make clear to the mind.
items.cn: illustrare 加强此义：把光照上去，引申为使心中明白。

items.en: Church writers used illustrare of famous men whose deeds lit up their age.
items.cn: 教会作家用 illustrare 形容功业照亮时代的著名人物。

items.en: English borrowed it as illustren, first meaning to enlighten or bring honour.
items.cn: 英语以 illustren 借入，最初意为启迪或增光。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the printing trade made to add pictures the everyday meaning.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，印刷业让「加插图」成了最日常的词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for making things clear.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁家族里的词；近义组收其他表示讲清楚的动词。

entries.definition: A picture or example that lights up a point.
entries.definitionCN: 插图或例证，用来把观点照亮。

entries.definition: Famous and admired, literally shining with light.
entries.definitionCN: 著名的、辉煌的，字面就是「发光」。

entries.definition: A soft shine on a surface, from the same light word.
entries.definitionCN: 表面的柔和光泽，同出光明一词。

entries.definition: To make something plain by giving reasons; broader than illustrate.
entries.definitionCN: 通过讲道理把事情说清楚，范围比 illustrate 更广。

entries.definition: To show clearly by doing or by proof.
entries.definitionCN: 通过演示或证据明确展示。

entries.definition: To remove confusion from a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 消除说法中的含混之处。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the light inside illustrare to pictures, examples and clear blackboard arrows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 illustrare 里的「光」连到插图、例子与黑板上清晰的箭头。

normal.en: The Latin root means light: to illustrate is to shine a lamp on an idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为光：illustrate 就是给一个想法打灯。

normal.en: The ill- here is not a negative prefix, so do not read it as not legal.
normal.cn: 这里的 ill- 不是否定前缀，别误读成「不合法」。

normal.en: The stress falls in the middle: il-LUS-trate.
normal.cn: 重音在中间：il-LUS-trate。

normal.en: -ate marks a verb, and its relatives are all nouns or adjectives of light and picture.
normal.cn: -ate 标示动词，它的同族词都与光和图画相关。

normal.en: A book with pictures is an illustrated book, so the verb keeps a footprint on every page.
normal.cn: 带图的书叫 illustrated book，这个动词在每一页上都留下脚印。

abstract.en: Explaining and drawing are two limbs of one act: both pull an invisible thought into the visible world.
abstract.cn: 讲解与绘图是同一动作的两条胳膊：都把看不见的想法拉进可见世界。

abstract.en: The word trusts the example more than the rule, because a lit case teaches faster than a definition.
abstract.cn: 这个词更信例子而非规则，因为被照亮的事例比定义教得快。

abstract.en: A single illustration can do what a whole paragraph cannot, which is why the picture stayed inside the verb.
abstract.cn: 一幅插图能做出整段文字做不到的事，所以图画一直住在动词里。

examples.en: The teacher illustrated the idea with a simple diagram.
examples.cn: 老师用一张简图说明了这个概念。

examples.en: This case clearly illustrates why the rules are needed.
examples.cn: 这个案例清楚说明了为什么需要这些规则。

examples.en: She has illustrated more than thirty children's books.
examples.cn: 她为三十多本童书绘制过插图。

dict_mnemonic.text: illustr 光（拉丁语「照亮」）+ ate 动词——把光照到想法上，就是阐明；配图也是照亮

root: 拉丁语 lustrare「照亮」→ illustrare「照亮、使明白」，中世纪拉丁语引申为增光，中古英语借入为 illustren，近代定形 illustrate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: to make an idea clear, to add pictures to a text, and to serve as a telling example.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：讲清一个观点、给文字配图，以及本身成为有力的例证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red chalk circle on a blackboard diagram, lighting up how a boat floats.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板示意图上被红粉笔圈出的一处，照亮船为什么浮。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM LINE: an example illuminates an abstract rule.
branches.cn: 课堂线：一个例子照亮一条抽象规则。

branches.en: THE PRINT LINE: drawings light up a page of text.
branches.cn: 印刷线：图画照亮一整页文字。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE LINE: a career or a case can be the example itself.
branches.cn: 证据线：一段经历或一个案例本身就充当例证。

branches.en: THE LIGHT LINE: all three keep the original image of throwing light.
branches.cn: 光之线：三个义项都保留「投光」的原意象。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT LINE: in essays the verb introduces proof, not decoration.
branches.cn: 论证线：在议论文里这个词引出的是证据，不是装饰。

intro.en: Illustrate is a Latin verb taken over almost whole, with English endings and a large family of relatives.
intro.cn: illustrate 几乎是整体搬来的拉丁动词，只换英语词尾，并带出一大串同族词。

latinIntro.en: The light root lustr- is recorded in Latin, and the prefix il- here is the preposition in-, not a negative.
latinIntro.cn: 表示光的词根 lustr- 有拉丁文献，这里的前缀 il- 是介词 in- 的变形，并非否定。

items.example: The root also hides in lustre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也藏在 lustre 里。

items.example: Create and activate behave the same way.
items.exampleCN: create 与 activate 也一样。
这张图说明了趋势。
她的经历说明了这种危险。

items.meaning: past form or describing a book with pictures
items.meaningCN: 过去式，或形容配有插图的书
items.exampleCN: 他买了一本插图指南。
每章配三幅插图。
这些数字只是示意性的。

items.example: The illustrator signed the first page.
items.exampleCN: 插画家在第一页签了名。

latinEntries.meaning: to light up, to make bright

definition_en: a picture in a book, or an example used to make something clear
core_image: 翻开的旧书页上，一幅钢笔画正对着它解释的那段文字
scene: 孩子翻到动物百科讲章鱼的页面。The illustration showed how the eight arms moved, and she read the text twice to compare.
sceneCN: 这里 illustration 是「插图、图解」（第 1 个义项：书中的图画），句意是插图展示了八条腕足如何活动，她把文字读了两遍来对照。画面里有翻开的书和钢笔画。

pos.zh: 名词：说明、图解、插图；例证

senses.title: A picture in a text
senses.definition: a drawing or photograph that appears in a book or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 出现在书籍或杂志中的图画或照片
senses.example: The manual has clear illustrations of each step.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册为每个步骤都配了清晰的图示。
senses.why: The noun of the light verb naturally covers the picture whose job is to light up the text.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自「照亮」的动词，自然指承担照亮文字之责的那幅图。

senses.title: An example that explains
senses.definition: a case given in speech or writing to make a point clear
senses.definitionCN: 在口语或文字中用来讲清道理的事例
senses.example: His failure is an illustration of poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 他的失败是计划不周的例证。
senses.why: Words can light things up as well as pictures, so the noun names an example used as a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 语言和图画一样能照亮事物，于是这个名词也指被拿来做灯的例子。

senses.title: The act of explaining or drawing
senses.definition: the work of explaining something or of drawing pictures for a publication
senses.definitionCN: 解释某事的工作，或为出版物作画的工作
senses.example: She earns a living from scientific illustration.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠科学插画为生。
senses.why: English often lets a -tion noun stand for the activity itself and for the trade built on it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让 -tion 名词兼指活动本身与由此形成的行当。

intro.en: Illustration is the Latin noun of lighting up, carried into English through French.
intro.cn: illustration 是拉丁语中表示「照亮」的名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Illustratio meant a shedding of light, both literal and figurative.
items.cn: 拉丁语 illustratio 意为投射光明，既指实光也指比喻的光。

items.en: In learned prose the noun came to mean the act of making a matter plain by words.
items.cn: 在学术散文中，这个名词转指用言辞把问题讲明白。

items.en: French used illustration for a comment that illuminated a passage of text.
items.cn: 法语用 illustration 指照亮某段文字的注释。

items.en: English borrowed the word with a sense of distinction or enlightenment.
items.cn: 英语借入时，词义偏向「显赫」或「启迪」。

items.en: Printed books brought the modern sense, a picture placed beside words that explain them.
items.cn: 印刷书籍带来现代义：伴随解释文字的图画。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers -ation nouns from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for pictures and examples.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的 -ation 名词；近义组收表示图画与例子的其他词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to light up or add pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，意为照亮或配图。

entries.definition: Famous and bright with honour, from the same light family.
entries.definitionCN: 声名显赫的，同出光明一族。

entries.definition: Lighting, physical or mental; a near twin of this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 照明、启示，是本名词的近亲。

entries.definition: A line drawing that shows how parts are arranged.
entries.definitionCN: 用线条画出部件结构的图。

entries.definition: Any painted or printed image; the widest word of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 任何绘制或印刷的图像，范围最广。

entries.definition: A case used to show a rule; the verbal rival of sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 用来展示规则的实例，是第二个义项的口头对手。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the -tion ending to the idea of a lamp beside a page of writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -tion 词尾与「文字旁边的一盏灯」这个意象连起来。

normal.en: Change the -ate of the verb to -ation and the action becomes a thing, a picture on the page.
normal.cn: 把动词的 -ate 换成 -ation，动作就变成了一样东西，即纸上的图。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: il-lus-TRA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音落在第三音节：il-lus-TRA-tion。

normal.en: An illustration can be a picture or an example; both are lamps for a page.
normal.cn: illustration 可以是图也可以是例，两者都是照在纸页上的灯。

normal.en: -tion is the busiest noun ending in academic English, so it fits a word used in textbooks.
normal.cn: -tion 是学术英语里最忙的名词词尾，正配教材里的词。

normal.en: Children's books are judged by their illustrations before their words are read.
normal.cn: 童书常先看图再读字，这说明插图的位置。

abstract.en: The page carries a meaning and the picture carries a second one, and the reader meets them in the space between.
abstract.cn: 文字带一层意义，图画带另一层，读者在两者之间的空隙里相遇。

abstract.en: An example in an argument is a lamp placed where the reader stumbles.
abstract.cn: 论证中的例子，就是摆在读者绊脚处的灯。

abstract.en: The word keeps two trades alive at once: the scholar's comment and the artist's drawing.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时养着两门手艺：学者的注释与画家的画。

examples.en: The dictionary is full of small illustrations in the margin.
examples.cn: 这本词典的页边布满小插图。

examples.en: By way of illustration, consider two students with the same marks.
examples.cn: 举例来说，看看两位分数相同的学生。

examples.en: Her illustrations made the science book easy to follow.
examples.cn: 她的插图让这本科普书容易读懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: illustrate 配图、阐明 + ion 名词尾——插图；例证

root: 拉丁语 lustrare「照亮」→ illustratio「照明、阐明」，经古法语 illustration 进入英语，近代定指书中插图与例证。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a picture inside a text, an example that explains, and the work of illustrating.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：文字中的图画、用来解释的例子，以及绘图或解释这项工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black-ink drawing facing the paragraph it explains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅钢笔插图正对着它解释的那段文字。

branches.en: THE PAGE LINE: books, manuals and magazines place pictures among words.
branches.cn: 纸页线：书籍、手册与杂志把图放进文字里。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT LINE: a failure or a case can stand as illustration.
branches.cn: 论证线：一次失败或一个案例就可充当例证。

branches.en: THE STUDIO LINE: scientific illustration is a paid craft.
branches.cn: 工作室线：科学插画是一门挣钱的手艺。

branches.en: THE ARTIST LINE: the illustrator's work ends up as an illustration.
branches.cn: 画家线：插图作者的工作最终落成一幅插图。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: pictures speak to the eye, examples to the mind.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：图对眼睛说话，例子对头脑说话。

intro.en: Illustration is a Latin light root plus the noun ending -ion, with a rich family of related forms.
intro.cn: illustration 是拉丁语光之词根加名词词尾 -ion，周围有一整套同族形式。

latinIntro.en: Lustr- and the ending -io are both documented in Latin; the English -tion is their regular descendant.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 lustr- 与词尾 -io 在拉丁语中都有记录，英语的 -tion 是它们的规律继承者。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根还造出 lustre。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: Action and creation follow the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: action 与 creation 遵循同样规律。

items.example: The illustration shows the whole engine.
items.exampleCN: 这幅插图展示了整台发动机。
这本图册收录了五十幅插图。

items.meaning: to add pictures or make clear
items.exampleCN: 他为自己的讲座画了插图。

items.example: It is an illustrative example, not a rule.
items.exampleCN: 这是个说明性的例子，不是规则。
这位插图作者用水彩作画。
一个显赫的家族曾住在这里。

definition_en: a picture of someone or something, or the idea that people have of a person or a company
core_image: 橱窗里一张被灯光打亮的人物海报
scene: 地铁通道的灯箱一夜之间全换了内容。The image of a smiling farmer held the same pose on every panel, so commuters looked twice.
sceneCN: 这里 image 是「影像、图像」（第 1 个义项：人或物的画面），句意是一位微笑农夫的照片在每个灯箱上都保持同一姿势，乘客忍不住多看两眼。画面里有地铁通道和发亮的灯箱。

pos.zh: 名词：形象、影像、图像；印象

senses.title: A picture of something
senses.definition: a picture produced by a camera, a screen or a mirror
senses.definitionCN: 由相机、屏幕或镜子形成的画面
senses.example: The screen showed a sharp image of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上出现了清晰的月球影像。
senses.why: The word entered English as a name for a copy of a thing, a shape standing in for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，本是指某物的复制之形，即代替实物存在的那个样子。

senses.title: The idea people have of someone
senses.definition: the impression that a person or organisation gives to the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或机构给公众留下的总体观感
senses.example: The firm hired a designer to rebuild its image.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘请设计师重塑形象。
senses.why: The picture in public minds is treated as if it were a picture on a wall, so the same noun serves for fame and reputation.
senses.whyCN: 公众心中的那幅画被当成挂在墙上的画，于是同一个名词也用来指声望与口碑。

senses.title: A word picture in art and poetry
senses.definition: a description or figure of speech that makes readers see something
senses.definitionCN: 让读者眼前浮现画面的描写或修辞
senses.example: The poem opens with an image of rain on an empty road.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗以空荡路上下雨的意象开篇。
senses.why: Literature borrows the visual word because a good phrase paints a picture inside the reader.
senses.whyCN: 文学借用这个视觉词，因为一句好话能在读者心里画出图来。

intro.en: Image comes from a Latin word for a likeness or a statue, and it still keeps that sense of a shape standing for something.
intro.cn: image 来自拉丁语中表示「相似之物、雕像」的词，至今仍保留「以形代物」的含义。

items.en: Imago was a likeness, whether a carved statue or the picture of a face.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 指相像之物，既可为雕像，也可为面容的图画。

items.en: Imaginem was the accusative form most often met in texts, and it gave the word to later languages.
items.cn: 宾格形式 imaginem 在文献中最常见，后来的语言正是从这里取词。

items.en: French shortened it to image, still meaning a copy or a figure.
items.cn: 法语把它缩为 image，仍指复制之形或人物形象。

items.en: English adopted the French form and used it for statues, paintings and pictures in the mind.
items.cn: 英语沿用此形，用来指雕像、绘画以及心中的画面。

items.en: Photography and later television widened it to any picture made by light or by a screen.
items.cn: 摄影与后来的电视把它扩展到一切由光或屏幕生成的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same imag- root; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns for pictures.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 imag- 为词根的词；近义组收其他表示画面的名词。

entries.definition: To form a picture in the mind, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中构出画面，同一词根。

entries.definition: Images as a group, especially in art or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 图像或意象的集合，尤用于艺术与文学。

entries.definition: A copy of something, built on a similar pattern though not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 仿制品，构词形式相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: A painting, drawing or photograph, the plainest everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画、图画或照片，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: An image made by light on film or a sensor.
entries.definitionCN: 由光线落在胶片或传感器上形成的影像。

entries.definition: The opinion others hold of a person, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 他人对某人的评价，与第二个义项相近。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the Latin statue imago to screens, mirrors and public faces.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语的雕像 imago 连到屏幕、镜子和公众面孔上。

normal.en: Drop the final e and you get imag-, the root that also grows imagine and imagery.
normal.cn: 去掉词尾的 e 得到 imag-，这个词根还长出 imagine 与 imagery。

normal.en: Six letters, stress the first: IM-age.
normal.cn: 六个字母，重音在前：IM-age。

normal.en: Soft g at the end, so it rhymes with village, not with cage.
normal.cn: 结尾的 g 发软音，与 village 押韵，而不与 cage 同音。

normal.en: A mirror gives a mirror image, and a screen gives a digital image; the word is always a copy.
normal.cn: 镜子给出镜像，屏幕给出数字图像；这个词始终是复制品。

normal.en: Companies worry about their image just as cameras worry about theirs: both are pictures seen by others.
normal.cn: 公司操心形象，正如镜头操心成像：都是别人看见的那幅画。

abstract.en: An image is never the thing itself; it is the thing seen from outside, frozen long enough to be looked at.
abstract.cn: 图像从不是事物本身，而是事物从外部被看见、并被冻住足够久以供注视的样子。

abstract.en: The word holds both a mirror and a reputation, because people build a picture of you and then live beside it.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装着一面镜子和一份名声，因为人们先为你画像，再与那幅画同住。

abstract.en: Every picture is a small promise that a thing can be held still, and every failure of that promise disappoints us.
abstract.cn: 每幅画都是一个小承诺：事物可以被定住；这个承诺一旦落空，我们就会失望。

examples.en: The telescope sent back clear images of the planet.
examples.cn: 望远镜传回了这颗行星的清晰图像。

examples.en: Her public image as a strict judge is not quite fair.
examples.cn: 她作为严苛法官的公众形象并不太公允。

examples.en: He tried to improve the image of the brand after the scandal.
examples.cn: 丑闻之后他设法改善这个品牌的形象。

dict_mnemonic.text: imag 像（拉丁语「雕像、形貌」）+ e——照出来的样子，即影像；别人心中的样子，即形象

root: 拉丁语 imago（宾格 imaginem）「相似之物、雕像」，经古法语 image 进入英语，现代扩展到摄影图像与公众形象。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a visible picture, the picture held in public opinion, and a word picture in art.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：可见的画面、舆论中持有的印象，以及文学艺术中语言绘出的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit poster of a face repeated along a subway wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：地铁墙上被灯照亮、反复出现的同一张面孔。

branches.en: THE LENS LINE: cameras, screens and mirrors all produce images.
branches.cn: 镜头线：相机、屏幕与镜子都在产生图像。

branches.en: THE BRAND LINE: a company's image is its face in public.
branches.cn: 品牌线：公司的形象就是它在公众面前的脸。

branches.en: THE PAGE LINE: poets build images out of plain words.
branches.cn: 纸页线：诗人用朴素的词造出意象。

branches.en: THE COPY LINE: both are pictures standing in for something else.
branches.cn: 复制线：两者都是以画代物的复制。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: whether on glass or in lines of verse, the target is the eye.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：无论印在玻璃上还是写在诗句里，目标都是眼睛。

intro.en: Image is a Latin root with a light English ending; its family spreads across verbs, adjectives and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: image 是拉丁语词根加轻巧的英语词尾，其家族遍及动词、形容词与抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Imago and its stem imagin- are recorded in classical Latin, so the family rests on solid ground.
latinIntro.cn: imago 及其词干 imagin- 在古典拉丁语中都有文献，这个家族根基扎实。

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 imagery 中。
图像模糊了。

items.example: The film is full of strong images.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片充满强烈的意象。
想象房间被刷成蓝色。
她的想象力填补了空白。

items.example: The poem's imagery is all water.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗的意象全是水。
他们试了所有想得到的方法。
脑成像技术进步很快。

definition_en: the ability to form pictures and ideas in the mind, including things that are not actually present
core_image: 深夜书桌上散开的草图，窗外的云被画成了飞鱼
scene: 作文题只有一行字，纸上却很快铺满了东西。Her imagination turned a bare classroom into a ship, and the whole class began to steer it.
sceneCN: 这里 imagination 指「想象力」（第 1 个义项：在脑中造出画面的能力），句意是她的想象把空荡荡的教室变成一艘船，全班开始一起掌舵。画面里有只写一行字的作文题和慢慢填满的纸。

pos.zh: 名词：想象力、想象、创造力

senses.title: The power to form pictures
senses.definition: the ability to create images and situations in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中造出画面与情境的能力
senses.example: Children need imagination more than they need toys.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子需要想象力胜过需要玩具。
senses.why: The -ation ending names the faculty itself, so the word points to an ability rather than to a single picture.
senses.whyCN: -ation 词尾命名的是能力本身，因此这个词指向一种本领，而非某一幅画面。

senses.title: Something invented in the mind
senses.definition: a product of the mind that has no basis in fact
senses.definitionCN: 头脑造出、并无事实依据之物
senses.example: The monster was pure imagination, he admitted later.
senses.exampleCN: 他后来承认那怪物纯属想象。
senses.why: A faculty word easily slides into the thing the faculty produces, just as writing means both skill and text.
senses.whyCN: 表示能力的词很容易滑向它所产出之物，正如 writing 既指写作技能又指文字。

senses.title: Creative power in art or science
senses.definition: the inventive power behind new designs, stories or theories
senses.definitionCN: 催生新设计、新故事或新理论的创造能力
senses.example: The vaccine grew from years of scientific imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗源自多年科学上的创造力。
senses.why: Inventing and picturing rely on the same act of seeing what is not there, so the word covers both art and discovery.
senses.whyCN: 发明与想象都依赖同一个动作——看见尚不存在之物，于是这个词兼指艺术与发现。

intro.en: Imagination is the Latin noun built on imaginari, to picture to oneself, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: imagination 建立在拉丁语 imaginari（在心中构想）之上的名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Imaginari meant to picture something to oneself, active mental seeing rather than mere copying.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imaginari 意为在心头构想某物，是主动的心里观想，而非单纯复制。

items.en: Imaginatio named the faculty that holds such pictures, discussed at length by medieval scholars.
items.cn: imaginatio 命名持有这些画面的能力，中世纪学者对此多有讨论。

items.en: French used imagination for the mind's picturing power, both serious and playful.
items.cn: 法语用 imagination 指心智造图之力，严肃与游戏皆可。

items.en: English borrowed it in the fourteenth century, first in medicine and philosophy.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，最初见于医学与哲学。

items.en: Romantic writers raised imagination to a creative force, and education took it as a core skill.
items.cn: 浪漫主义作家把想象提升为创造之力，教育也把它视作核心素养。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root's other noun-like forms; the near-meaning group gathers powers of the mind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的其他名词性形式；近义组收其他表示心智力气的词。

entries.definition: Pictures in art or writing, near in shape but not the faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术或文学中的意象，形状相近但并非能力。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind, an adjective where this word is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于心中的：本词是名词，它是形容词。

entries.definition: Full of imagination, the adjective built on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 富有想象力的，与本词同基的形容词。

entries.definition: The power to make new things, closer to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 创造新事物的能力，更接近第三个义项。

entries.definition: A scene invented in the mind, often pleasant and impossible.
entries.definitionCN: 脑中虚构的情景，常是愉悦而不可能发生的。

entries.definition: The making of something new, or something made up.
entries.definitionCN: 造出新事物，也可指编造之物。

normalIntro.en: The hooks place the -ation heavy ending beside the lighter verb and adjective forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把沉重的 -ation 词尾与较轻盈的动词、形容词形式并排放。

normal.en: Long words often mirror long ability: five syllables for a power that never runs short.
normal.cn: 长词常对应绵长的能力：五个音节，配一种用不完的本事。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: i-ma-gi-NA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音落在第四音节：i-ma-gi-NA-tion。

normal.en: Its verb is imagine and its adjective imaginative; the ending changes the word's role.
normal.cn: 动词是 imagine，形容词是 imaginative，词尾改变的是词的职务。

normal.en: The root imag- sits inside image, so the power is always about making pictures.
normal.cn: 词根 imag- 就在 image 里，这种能力始终与造画面有关。

normal.en: Say beyond imagination and you name a limit you cannot measure.
normal.cn: 说「超乎想象」，你命名的是一条量不出的界线。

abstract.en: Imagination is not the opposite of knowledge; it is knowledge reaching for what does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 想象并不是知识的反面，而是知识伸手去够还不存在的东西。

abstract.en: A child with a stick and a good imagination owns a horse, a sword and a whole kingdom.
abstract.cn: 一个拿着棍子、想象丰沛的孩子，同时拥有一匹马、一把剑和整个王国。

abstract.en: The word describes a power that grows when used and withers when denied, unlike almost every other faculty.
abstract.cn: 这种能力越用越强、越禁越枯，几乎与所有其他本领都不同。

examples.en: The story caught the imagination of readers everywhere.
examples.cn: 这个故事激发了各地读者的想象。

examples.en: She has a vivid imagination and draws monsters every day.
examples.cn: 她想象力丰富，每天都画怪物。

examples.en: Solving the problem required imagination as much as knowledge.
examples.cn: 解决这个问题既需要知识，也同样需要想象力。

dict_mnemonic.text: imagine 想象 + ation 名词尾——想象的能力，即想象力

root: 拉丁语 imaginari「在心中构想」（词干 imagin-）→ imaginatio，经古法语 imagination 进入英语，近代由文学与教育学定为「想象力」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the power to picture, the products of that power, and its creative force in art and science.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：造画面的能力、这种能力的产物，以及它在艺术与科学中的创造力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sketch pads under a lamp, with clouds redrawn as flying fish.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下摊开的草图本，云被改画成飞鱼。

branches.en: THE FACULTY LINE: the word names a lasting capacity of the mind.
branches.cn: 能力线：这个词命名心智中一种持久的本领。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT LINE: monsters and kingdoms are its output.
branches.cn: 产物线：怪物与王国都是它的产物。

branches.en: THE CREATIVE LINE: designs and theories grow from the same root.
branches.cn: 创造线：设计与理论也从同一根部长出来。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: teachers value it alongside memory and logic.
branches.cn: 学校线：教师把它与记忆、逻辑并列看待。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY LINE: the same power gives both the picture and the fake.
branches.cn: 边界线：同一种能力既给出画面，也给出假象。

intro.en: Imagination is the heaviest member of the image family, built with the Latin noun ending -atio.
intro.cn: imagination 是 image 家族里最重的一员，用拉丁语名词词尾 -atio 构成。

latinIntro.en: Both imaginatio and its verb imaginari are recorded in Latin prose, so no reconstruction is needed.
latinIntro.cn: imaginatio 及其动词 imaginari 在拉丁语散文中均有记录，无需构拟。

items.exampleCN: image 与 imagery 共用此词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或能力的名词词尾
items.exampleCN: explanation 遵循同样规律。
想象力造出了整台机器。
他们的想象各走各的路。

items.example: Imagine a city with no cars.
items.exampleCN: 想象一座没有汽车的城市。
那是个富有想象力的设计。
那条线是假想的。

items.example: The novel is rich in imagery.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说意象丰富。

definition_zh: 富有想象力的；有创造性的；虚构的；善于构想的
definition_en: showing or having a lively imagination, especially in making new ideas or works
core_image: 一把普通椅子被孩子改造成飞船，扶手上挂着纸做的控制杆。
scene: 美术课上，一个学生把废旧纸箱剪成城市、桥梁和会转的风车。Her imaginative model turned a cardboard box into a city with bridges and windmills.
sceneCN: 这里 imaginative 指「显示出丰富想象力的」（第 1 个义项：作品或人具备活跃的造像能力）；句意为她富有想象力的模型把纸箱变成带桥梁与风车的城市。可辨识物件：纸箱、剪刀、桥梁、风车、课桌。

pos.zh: 富有想象力的；有创造性的；虚构的

senses.title: Full of imagination
senses.definition: showing a lively power to form new pictures and ideas
senses.definitionCN: 显示出活跃的造像与构思能力
senses.example: Her imaginative model turned a cardboard box into a city with bridges and windmills.
senses.exampleCN: 她富有想象力的模型把纸箱变成带桥梁与风车的城市。
senses.why: The adjective adds a suffix meaning tending to, so it describes whatever tends to produce imagination.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词加上表示「倾向于」的后缀，因此描述倾向于产生想象的人或物。

senses.title: Creative in method
senses.definition: using original ideas rather than repeating a known procedure
senses.definitionCN: 采用原创观念，而非重复已知程序
senses.example: The team found an imaginative way to reuse the old pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 团队找到一种有创意的办法来再利用旧管道。
senses.why: Creativity and imagination overlap here: a new method must be pictured before it can be tried.
senses.whyCN: 创造与想象在此重叠：新方法必须先被想象出来，才谈得上尝试。

senses.title: Existing only in the mind
senses.titleCN: 虚构的；只存在于想象中的
senses.definition: describing something invented by the mind rather than observed in the world
senses.definitionCN: 描述由心智编造、而非在现实中观察到的某物
senses.example: The story takes place in an imaginative kingdom with two moons.
senses.exampleCN: 故事发生在一个有两轮月亮的想象王国里。
senses.why: An invented world is a product of imagination, so works that build one are called imaginative.
senses.whyCN: 虚构世界是想象的产物，因此构建这类世界的作品被称为富有想象力的。

senses.title: Good at devising new options
senses.definition: able to think of fresh possibilities when the obvious ones fail
senses.definitionCN: 在显而易见的办法失效时能想出新的可能
senses.example: An imaginative manager sees three uses for a dead afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一位善于构想的经理能从一个空闲的下午看出三种用途。
senses.why: The trait is applied to people, not works, when the point is the ability to keep generating options.
senses.whyCN: 当重点在于不断产生选项的能力时，这个词用于人，而非作品。

senses.title: Vivid and engaging in description
senses.titleCN: 描写生动的、引人入胜的
senses.definition: presenting something in a way that lets a reader picture it strongly
senses.definitionCN: 以让读者强烈想象到的方式呈现某物
senses.example: The guide gave an imaginative account of the market's smells.
senses.exampleCN: 向导对市场的气味作了生动的描述。
senses.why: A description can lend the reader another person's imagination, so the adjective moves from maker to text.
senses.whyCN: 描写能把作者的想象借给读者，因此这个形容词从创作者转到文本。

senses.title: Forward-looking in planning
senses.definition: able to picture a future state and plan toward it
senses.definitionCN: 能够想象未来状态并据此规划
senses.example: The proposal was imaginative enough to survive three budget cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提案足够有远见，历经三次预算削减仍保留下来。
senses.why: Planning needs an image of what does not exist yet, which is imagination put to practical use.
senses.whyCN: 规划需要尚不存在之物的画面，这是想象投入实际用途。

senses.title: Prone to fancy
senses.definition: habitually turning to invented scenes or stories, sometimes at the cost of practical attention
senses.definitionCN: 习惯性转向虚构场景或故事，有时以实际注意力为代价
senses.example: The imaginative child missed the bell, still inside a story.
senses.exampleCN: 那个爱幻想的孩子还待在故事里，没听见铃声。
senses.why: The same tendency has a distracted side, so the adjective can describe someone lost in invented scenes.
senses.whyCN: 同一种倾向也有分神的一面，因此这个形容词可描述沉入虚构场景的人。

senses.title: Belonging to imaginative art
senses.definition: relating to art or writing whose value lies in invention rather than factual record
senses.definitionCN: 指价值在于创造而非事实记录的艺术或写作
senses.example: The course separates imaginative writing from reportage.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程把想象性写作与报道写作分开。
senses.why: Schools label a whole domain by the faculty it exercises, so fiction and poetry become imaginative writing.
senses.whyCN: 学校用所运用的能力来命名整个领域，于是小说与诗歌成为想象性写作。

intro.en: Imaginative comes from Late Latin imaginativus, an adjective built on imaginatio, imagination, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: imaginative 来自晚期拉丁形容词 imaginativus，建立在 imaginatio「想象」之上，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Imago meant an image or likeness. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is not settled.
items.cn: imago 指图像或相似物。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: Imaginari meant to form an image in the mind, a verb built on the noun for image.
items.cn: imaginari 意为在头脑中形成图像，是由「图像」名词构成的动词。

items.en: The adjective imaginativus described what belongs to the image-forming power, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 imaginativus 描述属于造像能力的事物，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French imaginatif carried the adjective into English in the fourteenth century, alongside imagination and imagine.
items.cn: 古法语 imaginatif 在十四世纪把这个形容词带入英语，与 imagination、imagine 同时进入。

items.en: English later divided the family: imaginative describes creative power, imaginary describes what is not real, and imaginable describes what can be pictured.
items.cn: 英语后来把这个词族分工：imaginative 描述创造能力，imaginary 描述不真实之物，imaginable 描述可被想象之物。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and pre-Latin origin of image): the earliest citation is not firmly fixed, and the deeper source of imago is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与「图像」义的拉丁语之前来源）：最早书证没有定论；imago 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the three adjectives that English speakers most often mix up; group two holds near words for creative strength.
note.cn: 第一组是英语使用者最常混淆的三个形容词；第二组是表示创造能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind; an imaginary country is invented, but the adjective says nothing about whether the invention is good.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于心中；想象中的国度是虚构的，但这个形容词并不评价虚构得好不好。

entries.definition: Able to be imagined; it marks the limit of possibility, as in every imaginable colour.
entries.definitionCN: 能被想象到的；它标出可能性的边界，如每一种想得到的颜色。

entries.definition: The power or its products; imaginative is the adjective describing someone or something that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 能力或其产物；imaginative 是描述拥有该能力的人或物的形容词。

entries.definition: A visible or mental picture; imaginative work is full of images, but the two words are different parts of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 可见或心中的画面；富有想象力的作品充满画面，但这两个词词性不同。

entries.definition: Producing original works or ideas; imaginative stresses the inner picture, creative stresses the output.
entries.definitionCN: 产生原创作品或观念；imaginative 强调内心画面，creative 强调产出。

entries.definition: Skilled at inventing devices or solutions; it is close to imaginative but often more practical.
entries.definitionCN: 擅长发明装置或办法；与 imaginative 相近，但通常更务实。

entries.definition: New and not derived from something else; an original idea may or may not be imaginative in style.
entries.definitionCN: 新的、并非来自他物的；原创观念未必在风格上富有想象。

entries.definition: Guided by fancy rather than reason, often in a playful or unrealistic way.
entries.definitionCN: 受幻想而非理性引导，常带玩闹或不切实际意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the image root, the tending-to suffix and the three adjectives that split the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「图像」词根、表示「倾向于」的后缀，以及把这个词族分开的三个形容词。

normal.en: The word is imagination plus a suffix meaning tending to: tending to make images.
normal.cn: 这个词是 imagination 加表示「倾向于」的后缀：倾向于造像。

normal.en: The family split three ways: imaginative means creative, imaginary means unreal, imaginable means possible to picture.
normal.cn: 这个词族分成三支：imaginative 指有创造力，imaginary 指不真实，imaginable 指可以被想象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: imaginative writing, an imaginative solution, an imaginative child.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：想象性写作、有创意的解决办法、想象力丰富的孩子。

normal.en: The same root appears in image, imagery and imagine, all concerned with pictures.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 image、imagery 与 imagine 中，都与画面有关。

normal.en: A cardboard box turned into a city is the adjective made visible.
normal.cn: 一只纸箱变成一座城市，就是这个形容词的可见形态。

abstract.en: Picture a chair that has quietly become a spaceship without losing its legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子悄悄变成飞船，却没有失去它的腿。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase that turns into a river when no one is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯在无人注意时变成一条河。

abstract.en: Picture a lesson plan that folds itself into a paper bird and flies.
abstract.cn: 想象一份教案把自己折成纸鸟飞走。

examples.en: The most imaginative answer was also the cheapest.
examples.cn: 最有想象力的答案同时也是最便宜的。

examples.en: Her imaginative staging used only shadows and one lamp.
examples.cn: 她的舞台设计富有想象，只用影子与一盏灯。

examples.en: Children are often more imaginative with a plain box than with a finished toy.
examples.cn: 孩子面对一个普通纸箱，往往比面对一件成品玩具更有想象力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 脑子里装满画面，随手就能把旧东西想成新东西 → 富有想象力的

root: 拉丁 imago「图像」→ imaginari「形成图像」→ imaginatio「想象」→ 晚期拉丁 imaginativus；经法语 imaginatif 入英语为 imaginative。imago 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one tendency: a person or work tends to make images, and that tendency shows as creative method, invented worlds, practical resourcefulness, vivid description, foresight, daydreaming and a whole artistic domain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种倾向展开：人或作品倾向于造像，这种倾向表现为有创意的方法、虚构世界、务实的机变、生动的描写、远见、白日梦以及整个艺术领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ordinary chair wearing paper wings and a cardboard control stick.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把普通椅子装上纸翅膀和纸板操纵杆。

branches.en: THE TRAIT: the base sense is simply a lively image-making tendency.
branches.cn: 特质：基础义就是活跃的造像倾向。

branches.en: THE METHOD: new procedures and fresh options are pictured before they are tried.
branches.cn: 方法：新程序与新选项在尝试之前先被想象出来。

branches.en: THE INVENTED WORLD: fiction and imaginative art live in pictures of what is not.
branches.cn: 虚构世界：小说与想象性艺术活在「不存在之物」的画面里。

branches.en: THE DESCRIPTION: a text can lend its pictures to a reader.
branches.cn: 描写：文本可以把它的画面借给读者。

branches.en: THE FORWARD AND THE LOST: the same tendency can plan ahead or drift away.
branches.cn: 向前与走神：同一种倾向既能规划未来，也能飘走。

intro.en: Imaginative is an adjective of tendency built on the imagination family, which comes from a Latin word for image.
intro.cn: imaginative 是建立在想象词族之上的倾向形容词，该词族来自拉丁语中表示「图像」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin imago and imaginatio give image, imagine and imagination; the adjective suffix -ive then forms imaginative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 imago 与 imaginatio 提供 image、imagine 与 imagination；形容词后缀再构成 imaginative。

items.example: The image of the sea stayed with her.
items.exampleCN: 大海的画面留在她心里。

items.example: Imagine a city with no cars.
items.exampleCN: 想象一座没有汽车的城市。
想象跑得比预算快。

items.example: The design is imaginative and simple.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计富有想象又简单。
这个房间的灯光设计很有想象。
这部续集缺乏想象力。
那条边界是虚构的。
每一种想得到的借口都试过了。

items.example: The imagery is drawn from winter.
items.exampleCN: 这些意象取自冬天。

latinEntries.structure: imaginari, imaginatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_en: to form a picture of something in the mind, or to suppose that something is true
core_image: 闭上眼伸手在空中画出形状的那个人
scene: 培训师让全员先放下笔。Close your eyes and imagine the shop on a busy Saturday, she said, then write what the door sounds like.
sceneCN: 这里 imagine 是「想象、设想」（第 1 个义项：在脑中造出画面），句意是她让大家闭上眼想象周六热闹的店铺，再写下门的声音。画面里有放下笔的学员和空中画出的形状。

pos.zh: 动词：想象、设想；猜想、料想

senses.title: To form a picture in the mind
senses.definition: to create an idea or image of something in your thinking
senses.definitionCN: 在思维中造出某物的意念或画面
senses.example: Imagine standing on that bridge at sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 想象一下日出时站在那座桥上。
senses.why: The verb is the action version of the picture word, so it names the work of building an inner image on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是「画面」一词的动作版，指有意在内部造出图像的过程。

senses.title: To suppose or guess
senses.definition: to think that something is probably true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在无证据的情况下认为某事大概为真
senses.example: I imagine he is still waiting at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜他还在车站等着。
senses.why: When we cannot see, we build a picture and treat it as the truth, and the same verb covers that guess.
senses.whyCN: 看不见时，我们就造一幅画并把它当作事实，这个动词也顺带覆盖了这种猜测。

senses.title: Used to call attention
senses.definition: used at the start of a remark to invite someone to consider something surprising
senses.definitionCN: 放在话首，请对方设想某件意外之事
senses.example: Imagine my surprise when the door opened by itself.
senses.exampleCN: 想想我当时多惊讶，门自己开了。
senses.why: Inviting a listener to picture a scene is a quick way to share a feeling, so the verb became a rhetorical opener.
senses.whyCN: 请听话人构想一个场景，是分享感受的快捷方式，于是这个动词成了修辞式的开场。

intro.en: Imagine is the French-shaped verb behind the Latin noun for picturing, and it entered English before the noun did.
intro.cn: imagine 是由拉丁语「构想」名词派生、经法语塑形的动词，进入英语的时间比名词还早。

items.en: Imaginari meant to picture to oneself, a deliberate act of the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imaginari 意为在心中构想，是心智有意的动作。

items.en: The stem imagin- came from imago, a likeness or image of a thing.
items.cn: 词干 imagin- 源自 imago，即某物的形貌或影像。

items.en: French trimmed the ending to imaginer, keeping the present stem imagin-.
