items.cn: 法语把词尾削为 imaginer，保留了现在时词干 imagin-。

items.en: English took it over in the fourteenth century as imaginen, now spelled imagine.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 imaginen 借用，今拼作 imagine。

items.en: The word spread from philosophy into everyday speech, where imagine now often means simply suppose.
items.cn: 这个词从哲学走入日常口语，如今常只表示「猜想」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of thinking.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的各形式；近义组收其他表示思维的动词。

entries.definition: Not real, existing only in the mind; the adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实、只存在于心中的形容词。

entries.definition: The faculty this verb puts to work.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词所调用的那种能力。

entries.definition: To copy, close in shape and sound but from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿，形近音近但词根不同。

entries.definition: To think something likely; plainer than imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事可能，比 imagine 更平实。

entries.definition: To picture something as a future possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事设想为未来的可能。

entries.definition: To form a clear picture deliberately, often for training.
entries.definitionCN: 有意形成清晰画面，常用于训练。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the verb to closed eyes, Sunday guessing and the surprise opener.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个动词系到闭上眼、周末的猜测以及惊讶的开场白上。

normal.en: Image plus -ine gives the verb; keep the root and the meaning follows.
normal.cn: image 加 -ine 就是这个动词：留住词根，意思自然跟来。

normal.en: One m, one g, then the light -ine: i-MA-gine, stress the middle.
normal.cn: 一个 m、一个 g，再接轻读的 -ine：i-MA-gine，重音在中间。

normal.en: The magic word of every exercise: imagine the scene, then describe it.
normal.cn: 所有练习的起手词：先想象场景，再来描述。

normal.en: In speech it often means simply guess, as in I imagine so.
normal.cn: 口语里常只表示「猜」，如 I imagine so。

normal.en: The g is soft, so imagine rhymes with engine and machine, not with pine.
normal.cn: g 发软音，imagine 与 engine、machine 押韵，不与 pine 同韵。

abstract.en: To imagine is to lend reality a draft copy, so the mind can try the world before it commits.
abstract.cn: 想象是给现实递上一份草稿，好让心智在定稿之前先试一试世界。

abstract.en: The word can be a question or a lantern: suppose turns it into a guess, imagine a beginning of a story.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以是疑问也可以是灯：说 suppose 时它是猜测，说 imagine 时它是故事的开头。

abstract.en: Every plan, bridge and law was once something somebody merely imagined.
abstract.cn: 每一份计划、每一座桥、每一条法律，最初都只是某人脑中的想象。

examples.en: Imagine living in a house with no windows.
examples.cn: 想象一下住在一间没有窗户的房子里。

examples.en: I imagine she will arrive before lunch.
examples.cn: 我猜她会在午饭前到。

examples.en: Try to imagine how the villagers felt that morning.
examples.cn: 试着想象那天早上村民们的心情。

dict_mnemonic.text: imag 像 + ine 动词尾——在脑中造出相似的画面，即想象

root: 拉丁语 imago（词干 imagin-）「形貌」派生动词 imaginari「在心中构想」，经古法语 imaginer 进入英语，中古英语作 imaginen。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: building a picture, guessing without proof, and inviting someone to picture a surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：造出画面、无据而猜，以及请人设想一件意外之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with closed eyes drawing shapes in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：闭着眼、在空中描画形状的人。

branches.en: THE TRAINING LINE: exercises begin with imagine the scene.
branches.cn: 训练线：练习总以「想象这个场景」开头。

branches.en: THE GUESS LINE: I imagine so replaces I suppose so.
branches.cn: 猜测线：I imagine so 可替代 I suppose so。

branches.en: THE STORY LINE: imagine opens anecdotes of surprise.
branches.cn: 故事线：imagine 用来引出令人惊讶的逸事。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: in both, the mind supplies what the eye does not.
branches.cn: 心智线：两者都是心补上眼睛没看见的。

branches.en: THE SHARING LINE: the verb invites the listener inside a picture.
branches.cn: 共享线：这个词把听者请进一幅画里。

intro.en: Imagine is the lean verb of the image family: a Latin stem and a verb ending, with cousins for every part of speech.
intro.cn: imagine 是 image 家族里最瘦的动词：拉丁词干加动词词尾，各词性都有同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb imaginari and the stem imagin- are documented, and the French -er ending replaced the Latin infinitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 imaginari 与词干 imagin- 均有文献，法语的 -er 词尾替换了拉丁不定式。

items.exampleCN: image 保留同一词干。

items.example: Examine and combine end the same way.
items.exampleCN: examine 与 combine 词尾相同。

items.example: Imagine a room full of clocks.
items.exampleCN: 想象一间摆满钟的房间。
她总往坏处想。
他想象中的假期很安静。
别再处处设想危险了。
他们试了所有想得到的招数。
她的想象填满了整座房子。

definition_zh: 失衡；不平衡；比例失调；失调状态
definition_en: a state in which parts are not equal, or in which one side has too much weight, power or quantity
core_image: 一架天平一头沉下去，另一头翘起来
scene: 这里指「失衡」。 The report warns of a growing imbalance between what the city consumes and what it produces.
sceneCN: 这里 imbalance 是「失衡状态」（第 1 个义项：两端不相等）；句意：报告警告这座城市消费与生产之间失衡正在加剧。图中可辨识物件：倾斜的天平、一端堆高的货物、另一端空着的托盘。

senses.title: Two sides no longer equal
senses.definition: a state in which two parts differ in amount, weight or strength
senses.definitionCN: 两部分在数量、重量或强度上不相等状态
senses.example: There is a clear imbalance between the two budgets.
senses.exampleCN: 两份预算之间有明显失衡。
senses.why: Balance came from a two-pan scale. The prefix im- denies it, so the word paints the moment one pan sinks.
senses.whyCN: balance 来自双盘天平。前缀 im- 否定了它，于是这个词画出的是一头沉下去的瞬间。

senses.title: Trade running to one side
senses.definition: in economics, a persistent excess of imports over exports or of one region's surplus over another's
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中长期存在的进口大于出口，或一地区盈余高于另一地区
senses.example: The trade imbalance widened again last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 上季度贸易失衡再次扩大。
senses.why: The scale becomes national: goods flow one way and money the other, and the pans never level out.
senses.whyCN: 天平变成了国家尺度：货物流向一边，货币流向另一边，两只托盘始终不能持平。

senses.title: An ecosystem out of tune
senses.definition: in ecology, a disruption in which populations or resources no longer keep each other in check
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中种群或资源不再相互制约的紊乱
senses.example: Overfishing caused a lasting imbalance in the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 过度捕捞造成了礁区持久的失衡。
senses.why: An ecosystem is a set of scales linked together. When one pan drops, the others follow, and the whole arrangement tilts.
senses.whyCN: 生态系统是一组互相连接的天平。一只托盘下沉，其余随之而动，整个装置都倾斜了。

senses.title: Power weighted on one side
senses.definition: a situation in which one group holds far more power than another
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体掌握的权力远多于另一群体的局面
senses.example: The imbalance between employer and worker is structural.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主与工人之间的权力不平衡是结构性的。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from weight to authority. What tips the scale is no longer goods but the ability to set the terms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从重量移到权威。压翻天平的不再是货物，而是设定条件的能力。

senses.title: Charge or composition out of balance
senses.definition: in chemistry and physics, a condition in which ions, charges or components are not in the required ratio
senses.definitionCN: 化学与物理中离子、电荷或成分未达所需比例的状态
senses.example: An imbalance of ions changes the reaction rate.
senses.exampleCN: 离子失衡会改变反应速率。
senses.why: Here the scale is invisible but exact: the two sides must cancel, and the whole system registers every grain that does not.
senses.whyCN: 这里的天平看不见却精确：两侧必须相消，任何一粒没有抵消，整个系统都会记录。

senses.title: A body out of regulation
senses.definition: in medicine, a disturbance in the normal levels of hormones or other substances
senses.definitionCN: 医学中激素或其他物质水平偏离正常导致的紊乱
senses.example: The illness begins with a hormonal imbalance.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病从激素失衡开始。
senses.why: The body is described as a set of regulated levels. Illness is the pan that will not come back up.
senses.whyCN: 身体被描述为一组受调节的水平。疾病就是那只再也升不回来的托盘。

senses.title: A mind tipped off centre
senses.definition: an emotional state in which needs and responses are no longer in proportion
senses.definitionCN: 需求与反应不再成比例的情绪状态
senses.example: Loss of status can produce a lasting emotional imbalance.
senses.exampleCN: 失去地位可能造成持久的情绪失衡。
senses.why: The same scale is now internal. Feeling is weighed against circumstance, and the word records the tilt rather than naming a disease.
senses.whyCN: 同一架天平现在移到了内部。感受与环境被放在一起称量，这个词记录的是倾斜，而不是命名某种疾病。

senses.title: Load or proportion wrongly placed
senses.definition: in engineering, a distribution of weight or material that is not even
senses.definitionCN: 工程中重量或材料分布不均
senses.example: Engineers found a slight imbalance in the rotor.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师发现转子有轻微失衡。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense left: a rotating mass whose centre is not where it should be, so every turn shakes.
senses.whyCN: 这是保留得最字面的义项：一个转动体的重心不在应在之处，于是每一转都震动。

intro.en: Imbalance is im- 'not' plus balance, and balance is a pair of pans. Late Latin bilancia meant a two-pan scale, from bilanx, 'having two dishes'. The word therefore begins as an object on a merchant's table and ends as a description of economies, ecosystems and minds.
intro.cn: imbalance 是 im-“不”加 balance，而 balance 是一对托盘。晚期拉丁语 bilancia 指双盘天平，来自 bilanx“有两个盘子”。所以这个词最初是商人桌上的一件器物，最后成了对经济、生态与心理的描述。

items.en: Lanx meant 'dish, plate, pan of a scale'. Its own origin is uncertain; it may be connected with a root for 'broad dish', but no link is proved.
items.cn: lanx 意为“盘、碟、天平托盘”。它自身的来源不确定，可能与表示“宽盘”的词根有关，但未获证实。

items.en: Bi- 'two' plus lanx 'pan' gave bilanx, 'two-panned'. The Late Latin noun bilancia named the whole instrument and passed into French as balance.
items.cn: bi-“二”加 lanx“托盘”构成 bilanx“双盘的”。晚期拉丁名词 bilancia 指整件器具，进入法语作 balance。

items.en: French balance meant both the scale and the act of weighing. English borrowed it for the instrument, then for equality of weight.
items.cn: 法语 balance 兼指天平与称量行为。英语借入后先指器具，再指重量相等。

items.en: The prefix in- assimilates to im- before b, p and m. Here it is privative: it removes the balance rather than repeating it.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 在 b、p、m 前同化为 im-。这里是剥夺性的：它去掉平衡，而不是重复平衡。

items.en: Imbalance appears in English in the 17th century, first for physical scales, then for anything measured in two opposing parts.
items.cn: imbalance 在 17 世纪进入英语，先指实物天平，后指任何由两个对立部分构成的事物。

items.en: Trade imbalance, ecological imbalance and hormonal imbalance each extend the scale into a new domain. The word becomes a general diagnostic for systems that will not level.
items.cn: 贸易失衡、生态失衡、激素失衡把天平逐一扩展进新领域。这个词成了对“无法持平的系统”的通用诊断。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the base noun, its participle and the negative verb. The meaning group compares words for difference, unevenness and disturbance.
note.cn: 形近组区分基础名词、其分词与否定动词；词义组比较表示差异、不均与紊乱的词。

entries.definition: an even distribution, or to make two sides equal. It is the state that imbalance denies.
entries.definitionCN: 均匀分布，或使两侧相等。它是 imbalance 所否认的状态。

entries.definition: showing imbalance; not evenly distributed. It describes a thing, while the noun names the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 显示出失衡的；分布不均的。它描述某物，而名词命名该状态。

entries.definition: to make something lose its balance. It is an action, not a diagnosis.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物失去平衡。它是动作，而非诊断。

entries.definition: a large difference, especially in income or treatment. It stresses the size of the gap; imbalance stresses the failure to level.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大差异，尤指收入或待遇。它强调差距的大小，而 imbalance 强调无法持平。

entries.definition: an unfair difference in status, wealth or opportunity. It adds a judgement of fairness that imbalance need not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 地位、财富或机会上的不公平差异。它加上公平判断，而 imbalance 不必带此判断。

entries.definition: a lack of symmetry between two sides. It is structural and neutral, like imbalance in its technical senses.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧缺乏对称。它是结构性、中立的，接近 imbalance 的技术义。

entries.definition: an interruption of normal working. It fits the medical and ecological senses but suggests an event rather than a standing tilt.
entries.definitionCN: 正常运作被打断。它适合医学与生态义，但暗示某个事件，而非持续倾斜。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build imbalance from im- 'not' plus a two-pan scale, then let the sinking pan cover trade, ecology, power and the body.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 im-“不”加双盘天平搭起 imbalance，再用沉下去的那只托盘覆盖贸易、生态、权力与身体。

normal.en: See im- + balance: no balance. The word is simply the scale denied.
normal.cn: 看见 im- 加 balance：没有平衡。这个词就是被否定掉的天平。

normal.en: Picture one pan on the floor and the other in the air: that is every sense at once.
normal.cn: 想象一只托盘落在地上，另一只翘在半空：这同时就是所有义项。

normal.en: In trade, the sinking pan is the side that keeps buying more than it sells.
normal.cn: 在贸易里，沉下去的那只托盘，是买得多卖得少的那一方。

normal.en: In an office, the sinking pan is the side that sets the terms.
normal.cn: 在办公室里，沉下去的那只托盘，是能设定条件的那一方。

normal.en: Remember the word family: balance is the state, imbalance the failure, imbalanced the description.
normal.cn: 记住词族：balance 是状态，imbalance 是失败，imbalanced 是描述。

abstract.en: Keep one image: a straight beam that has forgotten how to be straight.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：一根忘了怎么变直的横梁。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a measurement, not an accusation: it tells you which side is heavy.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作测量，而不是指控：它告诉你哪一边重。

abstract.en: Notice that the same tilt can be repaired by removing weight or by adding it to the other side.
abstract.cn: 注意同一种倾斜可以靠减重修复，也可以靠给另一边加重修复。

examples.en: The trade imbalance between the two countries has narrowed.
examples.cn: 两国之间的贸易失衡有所缩小。

examples.en: A power imbalance makes genuine consent difficult.
examples.cn: 权力不平衡使真正的同意难以达成。

examples.en: The test checks for a hormonal imbalance.
examples.cn: 这项检查用来检测激素失衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“硬不懒死”：天平硬是不肯懒下来持平，一直斜着——这就是失衡。

root: im-（in- 的否定形式，在 b 前同化）加 balance；balance 来自晚期拉丁 bilancia“双盘天平”，源自 bilanx（bi- 二 + lanx 托盘）。lanx 的深层来源不确定，已标注。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses, one instrument. A beam with two pans appears as a budget, a trade account, a reef, a workplace, a solution of ions, a hormonal system, an emotional life and a spinning rotor. In each case the same thing has happened: the two sides that ought to cancel no longer do, and the whole structure leans.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项，一件器具。一根带两只托盘的横梁，先后化身为预算、贸易账目、珊瑚礁、工作场所、离子溶液、激素系统、情绪生活与旋转的转子。每种情形里发生的事都一样：本该相消的两侧不再相消，整个结构因此倾斜。

core.en: A scale that will not come level: one side carries more than the other.
core.cn: 一架无法持平的天平：一边承载得比另一边多。

branches.en: MECHANICS: unequal amounts and a badly placed load.
branches.cn: 力学：数量不等与载荷位置不当。

branches.en: ECONOMY: imports and exports that never level.
branches.cn: 经济：始终无法持平的进出口。

branches.en: NATURE: ecosystems and ions out of their required ratio.
branches.cn: 自然：生态与离子偏离所需比例。

branches.en: POWER: one side able to set the terms.
branches.cn: 权力：一方能够设定条件。

branches.en: BODY AND MIND: levels and feelings tipped off centre.
branches.cn: 身心：水平与情绪偏离中心。

intro.en: Imbalance is a negative prefix plus a borrowed noun. The items below show the scale family, the negation at work, and the adjectives that describe a tipped state.
intro.cn: imbalance 是一个否定前缀加一个借来的名词。下列条目展示天平词族、否定前缀的作用，以及描述倾斜状态的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the two-pan word and its parts. They explain why balance is not a simple English noun but a machine carried across languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“双盘”这个词及其成分。它们解释了为什么 balance 不是简单的英语名词，而是一台被跨语言搬运的机器。

items.example: The survey found an imbalance in staffing.
items.exampleCN: 调查发现人员配置失衡。

items.structure: French balance, from Late Latin bilancia
items.meaning: a two-pan scale; equality of weight
items.example: She kept her balance on the narrow beam.
items.exampleCN: 她在窄梁上保持了平衡。

items.example: The article gives a balanced account.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章给出了平衡的叙述。
这份饮食严重失衡。

items.example: One removed weight can unbalance the wheel.
items.exampleCN: 去掉一个配重就能使车轮失衡。

items.meaning: a weight or force that offsets another
items.meaningCN: 抵消另一重量的配重或力量
items.example: The second wing acts as a counterbalance.
items.exampleCN: 第二片机翼起配重作用。

items.meaning: to lose balance by excess, or to outweigh
items.meaningCN: 因过量而失去平衡，或重于
items.example: He overbalanced and fell from the ledge.
items.exampleCN: 他失去平衡，从台沿跌落。
配置均衡的投资组合能限制风险。

definition_en: to copy the way someone speaks, moves, or behaves, or to copy the style of something, often in order to learn it or to make people laugh
core_image: 客厅里小男孩照着爸爸刮胡子的动作，对着镜子抹一脸泡沫
scene: 晚饭后客厅里，男孩举着爸爸的剃须刷，学着大人刮胡子的样子挥来挥去。His little brother watched and tried to imitate every move.
sceneCN: 这里 imitate 是「模仿、仿效」（第 1 个义项：照着别人的动作或做法来），句意是弟弟在旁边看着，努力模仿他的每一个动作。画面里有晚饭后的客厅、一把剃须刷和一个学大人动作的小男孩。

pos.zh: 动词：模仿、仿效（某人的动作、声音、做法）；仿造、仿制

derivatives.zh: 无法模仿的、独一无二的

senses.title: To copy someone's actions
senses.titleCN: 模仿他人的动作或做法
senses.definition: to copy the way a person speaks, moves, or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 照着别人说话、动作或做事的样子来做
senses.example: Children often imitate the way their parents talk at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们常在饭桌上模仿父母说话的样子。
senses.why: The core of the word is copying, and people are the most obvious thing to copy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心就是「照抄」，而人是最容易被照抄的对象。

senses.title: To follow a style or model
senses.definition: to copy the style of a writer, artist, or product in order to learn from it
senses.definitionCN: 为了学习而照着作家、艺术家或产品的风格去做
senses.example: Many young painters imitate the old masters before finding their own hand.
senses.exampleCN: 许多年轻画家先仿效古典大师，再慢慢找到自己的笔法。
senses.why: Copying moves from the body to the work, and the aim becomes study rather than mockery.
senses.whyCN: 照抄从身体动作延伸到作品上，目的也从逗乐变成了学习。

senses.title: To make a false copy
senses.definition: to make something that looks like an expensive or original product
senses.definitionCN: 做出外形像正品或原作品的东西
senses.example: The market sells bags that imitate famous brands.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场上卖仿冒名牌的包。
senses.why: When the copied thing is a product rather than a gesture, the copying turns into imitation for profit.
senses.whyCN: 当被复制的是商品而不只是动作时，模仿就变成了图利的仿制。

intro.en: Imitate goes back to a Latin verb for copying, and its family has been describing copies for two thousand years.
intro.cn: imitate 源于拉丁语中表示「照抄」的动词，它这一族词两千年来一直在说「复制」这件事。

items.en: Imitari meant to copy or represent something, built on the image of following another's steps.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imitari 意为「复制、摹拟」，字面意象是跟随着别人的脚步走。

items.en: Imitatio was the noun for a copy or a likeness, and imitator named the person who made it.
items.cn: 名词 imitatio 表示「摹本、相似之物」，imitator 则指做这件事的人。

items.en: Old French took the verb as imiter, keeping the meaning of copying a model.
items.cn: 古法语吸收了这个动词，写作 imiter，仍表示「照着范本做」。

items.en: English borrowed it as imitaten in the sixteenth century, at first in the language of art and rhetoric.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把它借过来，写作 imitaten，最初多用于艺术与修辞的说法里。

items.en: The spelling settled as imitate, and the word widened from art to everyday behaviour and to goods.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 imitate，词义也从艺术扩展到日常行为，乃至商品的仿造。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same imit stem; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of copying.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 imit 词干的词；近义组收其他表示「复制、跟随」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of copying, or a copy that is not the real thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「模仿、仿制品」，指照做的行为或不是真品的东西。

entries.definition: Describing a person or thing that tends to copy others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「模仿的、爱仿效的」，形容人或事物喜欢照搬。

entries.definition: Close and private; it differs from imitate by one consonant and a very different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「亲密的、私人的」，与 imitate 只差一个辅音，意思却完全不同。

entries.definition: To make something exactly the same as another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「复制」，指做出和原件一模一样的东西。

entries.definition: To copy someone's voice or movements, often to make fun of them.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「模仿（声音、举止）」，常带有取笑意味。

entries.definition: To try to equal someone by copying their efforts.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「效法、努力赶超」，指靠模仿去追上别人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the Latin idea of following another's steps to the scenes where imitation happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语「跟着别人的脚步走」的意象，连到模仿真实发生的场景上。

normal.en: I + mitate looks like I meet a mate, and then I copy whatever the mate does.
normal.cn: i 加 mitate 看着像 I meet a mate，遇到同伴之后，同伴做什么我就跟着做什么。

normal.en: imitate and imitation differ only by the noun ending; the verb is what you do, the noun is what comes out.
normal.cn: imitate 与 imitation 只差名词词尾：动词是你做的事，名词是做出来的东西。

normal.en: Children imitate long before they can explain why, so the word describes learning by watching.
normal.cn: 孩子还不会解释为什么要学之前就已经在模仿，所以这个词说的就是「看着学」。

normal.en: A parrot that imitates your voice is not thinking; it is only copying sound.
normal.cn: 鹦鹉模仿你的声音时并没有在想，只是在复制声音。

normal.en: Doctors imitate the sleep of the patient when they follow a ward round: watch, then do.
normal.cn: 医生查房时的学习也是先看后做，正是「模仿」这条路的日常版本。

abstract.en: Imitation is how a culture stores a skill in bodies instead of in books.
abstract.cn: 模仿是文化把技艺存进身体、而不是存进书本的方式。

abstract.en: Every original style starts as an imitation that someone then pushed one step further.
abstract.cn: 每一种独创风格，最初都是一次模仿，只是有人又往前推了一步。

abstract.en: The same act is learning in a child and cheating in a market: the word does not judge, the context does.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作，在小孩身上是学习，在市场上却是欺骗：词本身不评价，语境才评价。

examples.en: He can imitate his teacher accent perfectly.
examples.cn: 他能把老师的口音模仿得惟妙惟肖。

examples.en: Young writers often imitate the authors they love before finding a voice of their own.
examples.cn: 年轻作者常常先模仿自己喜爱的作家，再找到属于自己的声音。

examples.en: Some birds imitate human speech with surprising accuracy.
examples.cn: 有些鸟模仿人说话，准确得令人惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: imit 照着做 + -ate 动词词尾——照着别人的样子做，就是模仿

root: 拉丁语 imitari「复制、摹拟」，由「跟随他人脚步」的意象而来；经古法语 imiter 在十六世纪进入英语，词义从艺术摹仿扩展到日常行为与商品仿造。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: copying a person's actions, following a style in order to learn, and making a false copy of a product.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：模仿他人的动作，为学习而仿效某种风格，以及仿制假冒的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small boy raising a shaving brush to a mirror and copying his father move for move.
core.cn: 核心意象：小男孩对着镜子举起剃须刷，一步一步照着爸爸的样子做。

branches.en: THE BODY: the copy lives in gestures, voices and habits.
branches.cn: 身体线：被复制的是手势、声音与习惯。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: imitating a style is how a beginner learns a craft.
branches.cn: 手艺线：仿效风格是入门者学手艺的路子。

branches.en: THE MARKET: imitation crosses into counterfeiting when money is involved.
branches.cn: 市场线：一旦涉及金钱，模仿就跨到了仿冒。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: imitate, imitation, imitative and imitator all hang on one stem.
branches.cn: 词族线：imitate、imitation、imitative、imitator 都挂在同一个词干上。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: inimitable says no one can copy this, which is a compliment.
branches.cn: 赞美线：inimitable 意为「无人能摹」，反而是句称赞。

intro.en: The affix table shows how the imit stem combines with verb, noun and adjective endings.
intro.cn: 构词表展示 imit 词干如何与动词、名词、形容词词尾组合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms imitari and imitatio sit underneath the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imitari 与 imitatio 是这一整族词的底子。

items.example: She imitates her sister's laugh without noticing.
items.exampleCN: 她没注意自己就在模仿妹妹的笑声。

items.meaning: the act of copying or a copy
items.example: The painting is a fine imitation of an old portrait.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是一幅很不错的古肖像仿作。
幼儿的模仿性极强。

items.example: The comedian is a skilled imitator of famous voices.
items.exampleCN: 这位喜剧演员是个模仿名人嗓音的高手。

items.example: Her inimitable style drew a large crowd.
items.exampleCN: 她那无可仿效的风格吸引了大批观众。

items.example: His jump remains unimitated in the league.
items.exampleCN: 他的那一跳在联赛中至今无人仿效。

items.example: Imitative learning shapes how infants pick up language.
items.exampleCN: 模仿式学习决定了婴儿习得语言的方式。

items.example: The boy stood by the window, imitating the conductor.
items.exampleCN: 男孩站在窗边，模仿着乐队指挥。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：摹本、相似之物

definition_en: the act of copying someone or something, or a copy made in this way
core_image: 一个人对着一面旧铜镜，把镜中人的动作一笔一笔描下来
scene: 博物馆商店里，一只古代陶俑被做成巴掌大的钥匙扣，价签上写明依照原件比例缩小复制。The label described the key ring as an imitation of the original figurine.
sceneCN: 这里 imitation 指「照原件做出的复制品」（第 3 个义项：物品的复制品）；句意为价签把这个钥匙扣称作原件小雕像的仿制品。

pos.zh: 模仿；仿制品；赝品；仿冒（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 模仿的；仿效的（由模仿词干加形容词后缀，表示具有模仿性质）
模仿者（由模仿词干加表示人的后缀，语义从行为落到人身上）
以模仿的方式（由 imitative 加副词后缀，把仿效性质转成动作方式）
模仿性（由 imitative 加名词后缀，指仿效的倾向或性质）

senses.title: The act of copying behaviour
senses.definition: the act of doing what another person or thing does
senses.definitionCN: 照着别人或别物去做的行为
senses.example: Children learn much of their speech by imitation.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童很大一部分语言是通过模仿学会的。
senses.why: Imitation starts with the eye: a model is taken in, and the hand or voice repeats it.
senses.whyCN: 模仿从眼睛开始：先接收一个样板，再由手或声音把它重复出来。

senses.title: Mimicry of a person
senses.definition: a performance that copies someone's voice, manner or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 复制某人嗓音、举止或外表的表演
senses.example: His imitation of the teacher made the whole class laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老师的模仿让全班都笑了。
senses.why: Here the copy is aimed at a person's style rather than at a thing, and the aim is often amusement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的复制对象是一个人的风格而不是物件，目的常常是好笑。

senses.title: A copy of an object
senses.definition: a thing made to look like another thing, often at a smaller scale
senses.definitionCN: 做成与另一件东西相像的物品，常常按比例缩小
senses.example: The shop sells imitations of the museum's ancient figurines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售博物馆古代小雕像的复制品。
senses.why: The copy now exists as a separate object beside the original, with its own price and its own label.
senses.whyCN: 复制品现在作为独立物件存在于原件旁边，有自己的价格和自己的标签。

senses.title: Counterfeit goods
senses.definition: a cheap copy made to be mistaken for an expensive original
senses.definitionCN: 廉价复制、用来冒充昂贵原件的赝品
senses.example: Customs officers found boxes of imitation handbags.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员查获了几箱仿冒手提包。
senses.why: The copy now hides its own origin; it does not stand beside the original but tries to take its place.
senses.whyCN: 复制品这时藏起了自己的出身；它不是站在原件旁边，而是想取代原件。

senses.title: Imitation as learning
senses.definition: in psychology, copying as a way of acquiring a skill or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，通过复制来习得技能或行为的方式
senses.example: The study measured imitation in infants watching an adult use a tool.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了婴儿观看成人使用工具时的模仿行为。
senses.why: Repetition is how a body learns: the learner copies first and understands later.
senses.whyCN: 重复是身体学习的方式：学习者先复制，之后再理解。

senses.title: Artistic mimesis
senses.definition: in art theory, the representation of nature or life by imitation
senses.definitionCN: 艺术理论中，通过模仿来再现自然或生活
senses.example: The debate over imitation in art goes back to the ancient Greeks.
senses.exampleCN: 关于艺术摹仿的争论可以追溯到古希腊。
senses.why: Art holds a mirror to the world; the copy is not a fake but a way of representing what is real.
senses.whyCN: 艺术给世界举了一面镜子；这里的复制不是造假，而是再现真实的一种方式。

senses.title: Social imitation
senses.definition: the copying of others' behaviour, fashion or habits across a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体里对他人行为、时尚或习惯的复制
senses.example: Fashion spreads through social imitation more than through advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 时尚更多靠社会性模仿传播，而不是靠广告。
senses.why: People copy in order to belong; the model is chosen because it looks like the group one wants to join.
senses.whyCN: 人们模仿是为了归属；选择这个样板，是因为它像自己想加入的那个群体。

senses.title: In imitation of; the proverb
senses.definition: used in the phrase in imitation of and in the saying that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示「仿照」的固定说法，也见于谚语「模仿是最真诚的恭维」
senses.example: The hall was built in imitation of a Roman bath.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大厅是仿照罗马浴场建造的。
senses.why: The phrase turns copying into a method, and the proverb turns it into praise: to copy someone well is to say they are worth copying.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把复制变成一种方法，谚语则把它变成赞美：把一个人模仿得好，等于说这个人值得被模仿。

intro.en: Imitation came into English around 1400 from Old French imitacion, from Latin imitationem, the noun of action from imitari 'to copy, portray'. The word first named the act and only later the object.
intro.cn: imitation 在十五世纪初从古法语 imitacion 进入英语，源自拉丁语 imitationem，是 imitari「模仿、描摹」的动名词。这个词先指行为，后来才指物品。

items.en: Imitari meant 'to copy, portray, imitate'. Its past-participle stem imitat- supplies the base of the English noun and its relatives.
items.cn: imitari 意为「模仿、描摹、仿效」。它的过去分词词干提供了英语名词及其同族词的词基。

items.en: The action noun imitatio (genitive imitationis) meant 'a copying, imitation'. English took the accusative form imitationem through French.
items.cn: 动作名词 imitatio（属格 imitationis）意为「复制、模仿」。英语经法语借入的是它的宾格形式 imitationem。

items.en: Old French imitacion carried the Latin noun into medieval French, and from there into English around 1400.
items.cn: 古法语 imitacion 把这个拉丁名词带进中世纪法语，又大约在十五世纪初进入英语。

items.en: The first English sense was 'emulation; act of copying'; the meaning 'an artificial likeness' is recorded only from around 1600.
items.cn: 英语最早的义项是「争胜、复制的动作」；而「人造的相似物」这一意思直到约十六世纪末才有记录。

items.en: Modern English uses the noun for copies, counterfeits, artistic mimesis and social copying; the adjective imitation is recorded from the nineteenth century, as in imitation leather.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个名词指复制品、赝品、艺术摹仿和社会性模仿；形容词用法从十九世纪起有记录，如「人造革」这一说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of imitari is not settled. Some accounts connect it with imago 'image, likeness', while others reconstruct a PIE root *aim- 'to copy'; both are proposals, and neither can be demonstrated as the single source.
items.cn: 来源不确定：imitari 更深来源尚无定论。一些解释把它与 imago「图像、相似物」联系起来，另一些则重构原始印欧语词根 *aim-「复制」；两者都是假说，都无法被证明是唯一来源。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close and are often mixed up with imitation; the second holds near neighbours that also name a copy, but with a different purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是与 imitation 形近或音近、常被混淆的词；第二组是同为「复制品」但目的不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb at the base of the family: to copy someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 这一词族的动词基础：复制某人或某物。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'copying or tending to copy'; it describes the tendency, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「模仿的、倾向于模仿的」形容词；它描写倾向，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: A restriction, from Latin limes 'boundary'. It rhymes with imitation but comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 限制，来自拉丁 limes「边界」。它与 imitation 押韵，但词根完全不同，两者并非同源。

entries.definition: A hint or indirect suggestion, from intimate 'to make known'. The shared ending is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示、间接提示，来自 intimate「使知道」。共同的词尾具有误导性，两者没有亲缘关系。

entries.definition: A general duplicate of an original; it carries no hint of deception or artistic theory.
entries.definitionCN: 原件的普通复制品；它不带欺骗或艺术理论的意味。

entries.definition: An exact copy, often made at the same scale and with official approval; it is more precise than imitation.
entries.definitionCN: 精确复制品，常按原尺寸并获正式许可；比 imitation 更精确。

entries.definition: A fake made to pass as genuine, especially money or goods; deception is built into the word.
entries.definitionCN: 冒充真品的假货，尤指钱币或商品；欺骗性写进了这个词本身。

entries.definition: The copying of another's appearance or behaviour, often for advantage; in biology it can help an animal survive.
entries.definitionCN: 复制他者的外表或行为，常为取得优势；在生物学中可帮助动物生存。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词语素、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: imit- (copy) + -ation (action noun): imitation is literally 'the act of copying'.
normal.cn: 复制词干加动作名词词尾：imitation 字面上就是「复制的动作」。

normal.en: Latin imitari 'to copy' and imitatio 'a copying' are the direct sources of the word.
normal.cn: 拉丁 imitari「复制」与 imitatio「复制行为」是这个词的直接来源。

normal.en: The family runs imitate, imitation, imitative, imitator, imitatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 imitate、imitation、imitative、imitator、imitatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the purpose: in imitation of, imitation leather, imitation goods, imitation learning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出目的：仿照、人造革、仿冒商品、模仿学习。

normal.en: The saying that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery is a fixed proverb, not a separate root meaning.
normal.cn: 「模仿是最真诚的恭维」是一句固定谚语，并不是词根另长出的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tracing the outline of a shadow on a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在墙上描出影子的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a copy that wants to be mistaken for the original.
abstract.cn: 想象一个希望被误认为原件的复制品。

abstract.en: Picture a child learning a knot by watching the same hands three times.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子看着同一双手打了三次结，才学会这个结。

examples.en: Young children learn language partly by imitation.
examples.cn: 幼儿部分通过模仿学习语言。

examples.en: The vase is a nineteenth-century imitation of a Greek original.
examples.cn: 这只花瓶是十九世纪对一件希腊原件的仿制品。

examples.en: His imitation of the manager's voice was painfully accurate.
examples.cn: 他对经理嗓音的模仿准确得让人尴尬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊米泰申」—— 伊米对着镜子学泰申的动作，越学越像 → imitation 模仿；仿制品

root: 拉丁 imitari「模仿、复制」，经古法语 imitacion 于十五世纪初进入英语。imitari 更深来源不确定：与 imago「图像」的联系属假说，重构词根 *aim-「复制」也只是提议，均无法定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one copying gesture: look, repeat, and make a double. The double can be a performance, a replica, a fake, a learned skill, a work of art, a social habit, or a phrase that turns copying into praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿同一个复制动作展开：看、重复、做出一个「另一个」。这个「另一个」可以是一场表演、一件复制品、一件假货、一项学来的技能、一件艺术品、一种社会习惯，或一句把复制变成赞美的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye takes a model, and the hand makes a second version.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛接收一个样板，手做出第二个版本。

branches.en: THE CORE: the act begins with a model outside the self and ends with a repeated action.
branches.cn: 核心：动作从一个自我之外的样板开始，以一次重复的行动结束。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE AS PERFORMANCE: the copy is aimed at a person's voice or manner and often played for laughter.
branches.cn: 作为表演的「另一个」：复制对象是一个人的嗓音或举止，常常是为了逗笑。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF OBJECT: a replica stands openly beside the original, while a counterfeit tries to take its place.
branches.cn: 两类物件：复制品公开地站在原件旁边，赝品则想取代原件。

branches.en: COPYING AS GROWTH: imitation lets a body learn a skill and lets a group share a habit.
branches.cn: 作为成长的复制：模仿让身体学会技能，也让群体共享习惯。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE IN CULTURE AND LANGUAGE: mimesis holds a mirror to nature, while a fixed phrase turns copying into a method and a proverb turns it into praise.
branches.cn: 文化与语言里的「另一个」：摹仿给自然举镜子，固定短语把复制变成方法，谚语则把它变成赞美。

intro.en: Imitation is a Latin action noun: a copying stem plus a very common noun ending, and the family spreads through verb, adjective, person and adverb forms.
intro.cn: imitation 是拉丁动作名词：复制词干加一个极常见的名词词尾，词族再向动词、形容词、人物名词和副词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is compact: a verb for copying, its action noun, and its past participle. English built the rest from the imitat- stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁这一族很紧凑：一个表示复制的动词、它的动作名词和过去分词。英语其余的形式都从这个过去分词词干长出来。

items.example: The stem carries the act of copying.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载着复制的动作。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing something
items.example: The ending turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成动作名词。

items.meaning: the act of copying; a copy
items.exampleCN: 博物馆出售复制品。
孩子会模仿听到的东西。
这种风格模仿性很强。

items.example: He is a skilled imitator of voices.
items.exampleCN: 他是个擅长模仿嗓音的人。

items.example: The child imitatively repeated the gesture.
items.exampleCN: 孩子模仿着重复了那个动作。

items.example: Researchers rated the imitativeness of each child.
items.exampleCN: 研究者评估了每个孩子的模仿性。

items.meaningCN: 无法模仿的；独一无二的
items.example: She has an inimitable way of telling a story.
items.exampleCN: 她讲故事的方式无人能仿。

模仿者（模仿词干加表示人的后缀，语义落到人身上）
以模仿的方式（imitative 加副词后缀，把性质转成动作方式）
模仿性（imitative 加名词后缀，指仿效的倾向）

definition_en: happening at once, or nearest in relation, with nothing in between
core_image: 手机屏幕上跳出一条消息和一个红色的立即回复按钮
scene: 客服台前的铃声响了一声，值班的人就转身接起。The patient's illness was immediate, so there was no time to look up the file first.
sceneCN: 这里 immediate 意思是「立即的」（第 1 个义项：不隔时间的），句意是那人的病情紧急，来不及先调资料。画面里有铃响一声就转身的值班人。

pos.zh: 形容词：立即的、直接的、紧接的

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: occurring without delay, with no waiting time
senses.definitionCN: 毫无拖延、没有等待时间地发生
senses.example: The medicine brought immediate relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这药立刻缓解了症状。
senses.why: The Latin prefix means without, and the root means in between, so immediate describes a gap that simply is not there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀意为「没有」，词根意为「中间」，于是 immediate 描述的是根本不存在的间隔。

senses.title: Direct and without a middle step
senses.definition: coming from or acting on something with no intermediary
senses.definitionCN: 不经中间环节地来自或作用于某物
senses.example: Smoking is an immediate cause of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟是这种病的直接原因。
senses.why: If nothing lies between cause and result, the link is immediate, exactly as the root says.
senses.whyCN: 若因果之间不夹任何东西，这条链就是「直接」的，正是词根所说的意思。

senses.title: Nearest in place or time
senses.definition: closest in the surrounding area or in the near future
senses.definitionCN: 在周边环境或近期中最靠近的
senses.example: The immediate area was cleared for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一带被清空了两个小时。
senses.why: The nearest ring around a point has nothing between it and that point, so the same word covers physical closeness.
senses.whyCN: 围绕一点最近的圈与那点之间没有东西，于是同一个词也覆盖了空间上的近。

intro.en: Immediate is built from Latin in-, not, and mediatus, intervened, so the word literally means with nothing in between.
intro.cn: immediate 由拉丁语 in-（不）与 mediatus（介入）构成，字面意思就是「中间没有东西」。

items.en: Mediare meant to be in the middle, from medius, the word for middle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mediare 意为居间，源自 medius，即「中间的」。

items.en: Adding in- produced immediatus, describing what has nothing standing between.
items.cn: 加上 in- 构成 immediatus，形容中间不夹任何东西的状态。

items.en: Schoolmen used immediatus of the direct relation between God and the soul.
items.cn: 经院学者用 immediatus 形容神与灵魂之间的直接关系。

items.en: In philosophy the word named knowledge received without proof or medium.
items.cn: 在哲学中这个词指不经证明或媒介而得的认识。

items.en: English took immediate broadly, for instant action, direct causes and the nearest circle of people.
items.cn: 英语广泛采用，用于即时行动、直接原因与最亲近的那圈人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the medi- middle root; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is prompt.
note.cn: 形近组收带 medi-「中间」词根的词；近义组收表示迅疾的词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, meaning at once.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，意为立刻。

entries.definition: Lying in the middle, the exact opposite of having no gap.
entries.definitionCN: 居于中间的，与「无间隔」正好相反。

entries.definition: A middle thing or channel, from the same middle root.
entries.definitionCN: 中介物或媒介，同出「中间」词根。

entries.definition: Happening in a single moment, often used of products.
entries.definitionCN: 一瞬间发生的，常用于产品。

entries.definition: Done quickly and without being late.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速且不拖延地完成。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything in between.
entries.definitionCN: 中间没有人或物隔着的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks open up the literal sense: no mediator, no gap, nothing in the middle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把字面意思摊开：没有中介、没有空隙、中间没有东西。

normal.en: Im- is not, medi- is middle, so immediate is not-middle, with nothing between.
normal.cn: im- 是不，medi- 是中间，所以 immediate 就是「不隔中间」。

normal.en: Compare intermediate: add the middle and you get the opposite.
normal.cn: 对照 intermediate：加上「中间」就成了反义。

normal.en: Four beats, stress the second: im-ME-di-ate.
normal.cn: 四个拍子，重音在第二：im-ME-di-ate。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and becomes the word on every emergency sign.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 成副词，就是每个应急告示上的那个词。

normal.en: Immediate family is the small circle with no relatives standing between you and them.
normal.cn: 直系亲属就是与你之间不夹旁人的那一小圈。

abstract.en: The word measures distance of a special kind: not metres, but the absence of anything in between.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量一种特殊的距离：不是米数，而是「中间空无一物」。

abstract.en: Direct causes and instant replies share one quality, the refusal of a middle step.
abstract.cn: 直接原因与即时应答共享一种性质：拒绝中间那一步。

abstract.en: Everything immediate is short-lived; the word names a moment that cannot be stored.
abstract.cn: 一切「立即」都短暂；这个词命名的是一刻无法储存的时间。

examples.en: The order takes immediate effect.
examples.cn: 该命令立即生效。

examples.en: His immediate reaction was to say nothing.
examples.cn: 他的第一反应是一言不发。

examples.en: Only the immediate family was invited to the ceremony.
examples.cn: 只有直系亲属受邀参加仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + medi 中间 + ate——中间不隔任何东西：立即的；直接的

root: 拉丁语 medius「中间」→ mediare「居间」，加否定 in- 成 immediatus，近代进入英语作 immediate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: no delay in time, no step in between, and no distance around.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：时间上不拖延、环节上不夹中介、空间上紧邻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flashing message with a red reply button waiting to be pressed.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上闪烁的消息和待按的红色回复键。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: immediate relief and immediate effect share a zero delay.
branches.cn: 时钟线：立刻缓解与立即生效都是零延迟。

branches.en: THE CHAIN LINE: an immediate cause needs no link before it.
branches.cn: 链条线：直接原因前面不需要再加一环。

branches.en: THE RING LINE: the immediate area and the immediate family are the closest ring.
branches.cn: 圆圈线：附近一带与直系亲属都是最内那一圈。

branches.en: THE GAP LINE: both senses depend on the same missing middle.
branches.cn: 间隙线：两种用法都依赖同一个「缺席的中间」。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST LINE: intermediate words do the opposite job.
branches.cn: 对照线：带 intermediate 的词正做相反的事。

intro.en: Immediate is a prefix plus a middle root plus a participle ending, a clean case of literal meaning surviving.
intro.cn: immediate 是前缀、中间词根与分词词尾的组合，字面义至今完好。

latinIntro.en: Medius and the negative in- are standard Latin, and immediatus is attested in later Latin.
latinIntro.cn: medius 与否定前缀 in- 是标准拉丁成分，immediatus 在后世拉丁文献中可见。

items.exampleCN: impossible 用同一否定前缀。
medium 与 mediate 共用此根。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，表示具备某性质
items.exampleCN: moderate 用法类似。

items.meaningCN: 不隔中间，立即的、直接的
items.exampleCN: 给我一个立即的回答。
立刻离开。
现场广播有即时感。

items.example: An intermediate class runs on Fridays.
items.exampleCN: 周五有中级班。
调解人与双方都见了面。

definition_en: at once, without any delay, or directly and with nothing in between
core_image: 救护车门一开，担架立刻被推进走廊
scene: 值班护士在门口听见刹车声，手上的记录本还没合上就站了起来。As soon as the bell rang, she went immediately to the ward without asking who called.
sceneCN: 这里 immediately 是「立即、马上」（第 1 个义项：毫无延迟），句意是铃一响她立刻去了病房，没问是谁按的。画面里有救护车的刹车声和还没合上的记录本。

senses.title: At once
senses.definition: in the very next moment, without waiting
senses.definitionCN: 在紧接着的一刻，不作等待
senses.example: Call the doctor immediately.
senses.exampleCN: 立刻叫医生。
senses.why: The -ly adverb keeps the literal sense of no gap and applies it to time.
senses.whyCN: 加 -ly 的副词保留「无间隔」的字面义，并把它用于时间。

senses.title: Directly, with nothing between
senses.definition: coming next in order or connected without a middle step
senses.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接，或不经中间环节地相连
senses.example: The library is immediately next to the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆就挨着礼堂。
senses.why: The same missing gap that removes waiting time also removes distance and intermediate steps.
senses.whyCN: 那个消失的间隔既能省去等待时间，也能省去距离与中间环节。

senses.title: Used for emphasis in speech
senses.definition: used to stress that someone did or refused something without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 强调某人毫不迟疑地做了或拒绝了某事
senses.example: She immediately said no to the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她一口就回绝了这个提议。
senses.why: Speech loves to mark a zero gap in reaction, and so the adverb also reports instant decisions.
senses.whyCN: 口语爱标记反应上的零间隔，因此这个副词也用来报告瞬间的决定。

intro.en: Immediately is immediate plus the Old English -lice, the ancestor of -ly.
intro.cn: immediately 是 immediate 加古英语词尾 -lice，即今日 -ly 的前身。

items.en: Immediatus already described relation without a middle term.
items.cn: 拉丁语 immediatus 已描述不带中间项的关系。

items.en: Adverbial forms like immediate stood beside the adjective in philosophical Latin.
items.cn: 在哲学拉丁语中，immediate 这类副词形式与形容词并列使用。

items.en: French used immediatement, shaping the adverb on the French pattern.
items.cn: 法语以 immediatement 的形式塑造副词。

items.en: English added its own -lice to the borrowed adjective, giving immediately.
items.cn: 英语给借来的形容词加上本土 -lice，形成 immediately。

items.en: The word became a standard instruction in medicine, law and notices.
items.cn: 这个词成了医学、法律与告示中的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and its middle-root cousins; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of haste.
note.cn: 形近组收该形容词及带「中间」词根的相关词；近义组收表示急促的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind this adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 本副词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: In a middle position, the reverse of the gap being gone.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中间地，与「无间隔」相反。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, often confused in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 先前地，快读时常被混淆。

entries.definition: In a single instant, often with a hint of magic.
entries.definitionCN: 一瞬间地，常带一点神奇色彩。

entries.definition: A plain phrase for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的朴素说法。

entries.definition: Without delay, common in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 不耽搁，日常口语常用。

normalIntro.en: The hooks carry the missing middle from the adjective straight into the adverb ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把形容词里那个「缺席的中间」直接带进副词词尾。

normal.en: Take immediate and add -ly; the -ly says it answers the question when.
normal.cn: 在 immediate 后加 -ly：这个词尾说明它回答「何时」。

normal.en: Five beats, stress the second: im-ME-di-ate-ly.
normal.cn: 五个拍子，重音在第二：im-ME-di-ate-ly。

normal.en: Long words can still be urgent, and this one sits on every emergency sign.
normal.cn: 长词也能万分紧急，这个词就站在每个应急告示上。

normal.en: Pair it with after or before: immediately after the meeting, immediately before dawn.
normal.cn: 常与 after 或 before 搭配：会后立即、天亮前马上。

normal.en: Not immediately obvious is the polite way of saying very hard to see.
normal.cn: not immediately obvious 是「很难看出来」的客气说法。

abstract.en: The adverb measures a gap that is not there, and in doing so it refuses every excuse of delay.
abstract.cn: 这个副词所量的是并不存在的间隙，因此它拒绝一切拖延的借口。

abstract.en: In medicine the word saves lives, and in a queue it starts quarrels.
abstract.cn: 在急诊里这个词救人，在排队时它惹人争吵。

abstract.en: Immediately is the closest English comes to naming a moment that has no length.
abstract.cn: 在英语里，immediately 最接近命名一个没有长度的瞬间。

examples.en: Please reply immediately if you receive the notice.
examples.cn: 收到通知请立即回复。

examples.en: The stairs are immediately to your left.
examples.cn: 楼梯就在你左手边。

examples.en: It was not immediately clear why the flight was delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误的原因一时并不清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: immediate 立即的 + ly 副词尾——立即、马上；紧接地

root: immediate（拉丁语 in-「不」+ mediatus「居间」，即中间无隔）加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: no delay in time, direct connection in place or order, and emphatic instant response.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：时间上不拖延、地点或次序上直接相连，以及强调毫不迟疑的反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretcher wheeled straight down a corridor the moment the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，担架便被径直推进走廊。

branches.en: THE EMERGENCY LINE: call the doctor immediately is a life-saving instruction.
branches.cn: 急救线：「立刻叫医生」是救命的指令。

branches.en: THE MAP LINE: immediately next to marks a position with no gap.
branches.cn: 地图线：紧挨着表示不留空隙的位置。

branches.en: THE CONVERSATION LINE: immediately said no marks a decision without pause.
branches.cn: 对话线：一口回绝标记的是没有停顿的决定。

branches.en: THE GAP LINE: both senses come straight from the Latin word for middle.
branches.cn: 间隙线：两种用法都直接源自拉丁语的「中间」。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: signs and regulations use it to forbid waiting.
branches.cn: 告示线：告示与规章用它来禁止等待。

intro.en: Immediately is a Latin-derived adjective with a native adverb ending, a very common English hybrid.
intro.cn: immediately 是拉丁来源的形容词加本土副词词尾，是极常见的英式混搭。

latinIntro.en: The negative prefix and the middle root are Latin, while the -ly is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀与「中间」词根来自拉丁语，而 -ly 属日耳曼语。

items.exampleCN: immortal 也用这一前缀。
mediate 带同一词根。
需要一个立即的决定。
灯立刻灭了。

items.meaning: in a certain way or at a certain time
items.meaningCN: 副词词尾，表方式或时间
items.example: Quickly and lately both use it.
items.exampleCN: quickly 与 lately 都用它。
这篇报道很有现场感。
需要一个中间步骤。

items.exampleCN: 调解人最后发言。
